meta.source: Memory Alpha (memory-alpha.fandom.com), CC BY-NC; curated overlays

records.lg: Enterprise arrives in a 1944 where the alien Na'kuhl have helped Nazi Germany invade America, and Archer, escaping capture, joins the Resistance in occupied New York.
With Silik as an unlikely ally, Archer strikes at Vosk's time conduit, and its destruction restores history and ends the Temporal Cold War.
Researching history in 1968, the Enterprise crew runs into Gary Seven, an agent of unseen aliens, as he and his cat Isis sabotage an orbital nuclear warhead launch.
The old guard crosses paths with a new generation, and bruised feelings and short tempers follow in a brief comic sketch.
Picard turns to a younger Guinan and meets Tallinn, the Watcher, while Rios is detained by immigration agents and Jurati strikes a bargain with the Borg Queen.
Renée Picard, an astronaut bound for Europa and Picard's ancestor, proves key to the altered timeline, as Q manipulates Adam Soong and Seven and Raffi spring Rios.
Tallinn enters a comatose Picard's mind to help him face memories of his mother, while Seven and Raffi hunt Jurati and Rios hides his origins from Teresa.
The crew sneaks into a pre-launch gala to shield astronaut Renée Picard from harm, with a Borg-influenced Jurati stealing the show, while Kore Soong uncovers her father's experiments.
Picard and Guinan must talk their way out of FBI custody before the Europa launch, while Seven and Raffi confront a Jurati now merging with the Borg Queen.
A Borg collective led by the Jurati-Queen hybrid besieges Château Picard, where Picard faces his mother's death, and Jurati ultimately leaves Earth to remake the Borg.
Racing the Europa launch clock, Picard saves Renée from Adam Soong, learns why a dying Q brought him here, and returns to 2401, leaving Rios behind in 2024.
Earth's first warp-five starship, Enterprise, launches early under Captain Archer to return a wounded Klingon courier home, and runs into the Suliban Cabal and a temporal cold war.
Enterprise finds an Axanar ship whose crew has been drained of a valuable fluid, and a doubting Hoshi Sato must master the Axanar language when the killers return.
Camping on the first Earth-like planet Enterprise finds, the landing party is exposed to hallucinogenic pollen, and a paranoid Trip becomes convinced T'Pol is plotting with rock creatures.
Helping repair a stalled Xyrillian ship, Trip Tucker plays a mental game with its engineer Ah'Len and returns pregnant, sending Archer to the Klingons for help finding her.
At Terra Nova, Earth's first colony, silent for decades, Enterprise finds survivors' descendants underground, blaming Earth for poisoned rain that actually came from an asteroid strike.
Visiting the Vulcan monastery at P'Jem, Archer's party is taken hostage by Andorians under Shran, who insist it hides a spy post, and Archer finds they are right.
Shadowed by a Vulcan ship, Enterprise sends Reed and Mayweather to sample a comet, where a mishap strands their shuttlepod, while Trip learns of T'Pol's arranged marriage.
Disguised as locals on a pre-warp world, Archer's team traces a mysterious illness to Malurians secretly poisoning the water, and Archer teams up with a local woman, Riaan.
Sent to aid the freighter Fortunate after a Nausicaan raid, Archer finds its resentful acting captain secretly holding a pirate prisoner and bent on revenge.
Silent aliens of unknown purpose attack Enterprise, forcing Reed and Trip to rush unfinished phase cannons online, while Hoshi hunts for Reed's favorite food for his birthday.
Crewman Daniels reveals to Archer that he is an agent from the future, hunting the Suliban Silik, who has slipped aboard among a group of alien pilgrims.
Phlox finds a cure for the genetic plague killing the Valakians, but he and Archer withhold it so the planet's other species, the Menk, can evolve unhindered.
Reed, Hoshi, and T'Pol board a crippled Klingon ship sinking into a gas giant and try to rescue its hostile crew as their own shuttlepod is stolen.
The Vulcans blame Archer for P'Jem's destruction and recall T'Pol, but on Coridan the two are taken by rebels, and after Shran helps free them, the Vulcans relent.
Mistaking debris for Enterprise's wreckage, Trip and Reed drift in a shuttlepod with dwindling air, bickering and bonding as they prepare to die, though the ship is intact.
Enterprise meets the V'tosh ka'tur, Vulcans who have embraced emotion, and T'Pol's cautious exploration ends when their member Tolaris forces a mind meld on her.
On the sunless rogue planet Dakala, visions of a woman lead Archer to a shape-shifting species hunted for sport by the Eska, and he helps it escape them.
Ferengi raiders knock out the crew and loot Enterprise, and Trip, spared because he was in decontamination, must stop them in little more than his underwear.
The derelict ship Enterprise salvages is home to Ezral, a survivor who has recreated his dead crewmates as holograms, and his very real daughter, Liana.
Straying into Tandaran space, Archer and Mayweather are held in an internment camp for Suliban civilians and, convinced of the detainees' innocence, help them break out.
A web-spinning creature that slipped aboard during a tense Kreetassan visit snares Archer and others, and Hoshi works to communicate with it before the captives die.
Archer ferries Vulcan Ambassador V'Lar, expelled from Mazar for alleged misconduct, as Mazarite ships give chase, and T'Pol's faith is rewarded when the charges prove a smear.
Zobral, grateful for repairs, hosts Archer and Trip on his desert world but wants their help in his rebellion, leaving the pair stranded in searing heat under fire.
Shore leave on Risa goes awry as Trip and Reed are robbed by shape-shifters, Archer's new companion hides an agenda, and an injured Travis needs a hibernating Phlox.
After a shuttle launch seemingly wipes out a mining colony, Enterprise is recalled, until Daniels exposes Suliban sabotage and Archer is stranded with him in a ruined future.
Stranded with Daniels in a devastated 31st century, Archer struggles to reach home while T'Pol's crew, held by the Suliban, fights to retake Enterprise and bring him back.
Over dinner, T'Pol recounts how her great-grandmother T'Mir and two fellow Vulcans, stranded in 1957 Carbon Creek, Pennsylvania, passed as humans and came to care for the town.
Enterprise hits a cloaked Romulan mine, and a second one latched to the hull pins Reed as he tries to defuse it, forcing Archer to cut him free.
An automated repair station fixes Enterprise with suspicious ease, then fakes Mayweather's death to harvest his brain for its computer network, forcing the crew to rescue him.
Archer frets through a night in sickbay beside Porthos, felled by an alien pathogen, while trying to mend relations with the Kreetassans, whom the dog has offended.
Enterprise finds a mining colony extorted for its deuterium by Klingon raiders, and the crew trains the settlers to fight back, turning their fuel into a fiery trap.
T'Pol asks Archer to help her capture Menos, a Vulcan agent gone rogue for two decades, a mission that unlocks memories she had suppressed of an earlier killing.
Reed's forgotten communicator draws him and Archer back to a pre-warp world, where they are caught and condemned as spies until Trip arrives in a Suliban cell ship.
Near a black hole, radiation drives the crew into obsessions, from Archer's writing to Trip's redesign of the captain's chair, leaving an unaffected T'Pol to save the ship.
After her first transport, Hoshi seems to fade from the crew's sight and uncovers aliens planting a bomb, all in the seconds before her body rematerializes.
Helping repair an alien ship, Trip wakes Kaitaama, a royal abducted for ransom and held in stasis, and ends up stranded with her on a remote planet.
Sheltering from a lethal neutronic storm, the crew crams into a warp nacelle's catwalk for eight days, until Takret militia board the seemingly abandoned ship.
Shot down by an Arkonian pilot, Trip is stranded with him on a moon whose sunrise brings lethal heat, and the rivals must overcome distrust to survive.
Vulcans threaten T'Pol's post on Enterprise on learning she has Pa'nar Syndrome, a disease they link to shunned mind-melders, while Phlox's wife Feezal flirts with Trip.
Shran asks Archer to mediate a standoff with the Vulcans over the disputed planetoid Weytahn, and Archer must get past a hotheaded Andorian lieutenant to broker a truce.
Enterprise recovers a tiny time ship, larger inside than out, with a dead human pilot, and is caught between the Suliban and the Tholians, who both want it.
Wrongly arrested by the Enolians, Archer and Trip are shipped toward the penal colony Canamar, and when a fellow prisoner hijacks the transport, Archer must outwit him.
A huge vessel swallows Enterprise, and its noncorporeal occupants begin swapping places with crew members, including Trip, until T'Pol's disciplined mind and Phlox help drive them out.
A Klingon tribunal tries Archer for aiding rebels, and despite the aging advocate Kolos's defense he is sentenced to Rura Penthe, from which Enterprise must spring him.
After his father's death, Travis visits the family freighter Horizon, where he clashes with his brother Paul, now captain, before helping the crew fend off raiders.
While Trip, Reed, and Mayweather descend caverns to evacuate Denobulan scientists from Xantoras, Phlox treats an Antaran patient who refuses care from a Denobulan.
Trip secretly teaches a Vissian cogenitor, a third-gender being treated as property, to read, and when Archer denies it asylum, it takes its own life.
Frozen Borg drones unearthed in the Arctic revive, assimilate their discoverers, and seize a ship, and Enterprise stops them only after they signal the Delta Quadrant.
News of A.G. Robinson's death leads Archer to recount their rivalry as NX test pilots, including the unauthorized flight that broke the warp two barrier.
Tellarite bounty hunter Skalaar abducts Archer to claim a Klingon reward, as a microbe sends T'Pol into pon farr while she is sealed in decon with Phlox.
An alien probe kills seven million from Florida to Venezuela, and Enterprise, reinforced with MACO troops, heads into the Delphic Expanse to stop the Xindi from striking again.
A freighter captain's tip sends Archer and Trip to a mining colony, where a Xindi laborer trades information for escape, a deal that goes badly wrong.
Battered by spatial anomalies, Enterprise is looted by Osaarian pirates, and a hardened Archer threatens a captive in an airlock to track down the stolen supplies.
A virus transforms Archer, Reed, and Hoshi into members of a long-extinct species, compelled to seek its lost city, as Phlox works on a cure.
Archer rescues Rajiin from an alien slave market, but the refugee is a Xindi agent gathering biological data on humans, and Xindi soldiers board Enterprise to retrieve her.
Inside an asteroid field, Enterprise finds the Vulcan ship Seleya crewed by maddened, zombielike Vulcans, and T'Pol begins succumbing to the same trellium-D poisoning.
The telepath Tarquin offers to help find the Xindi weapon if Hoshi keeps him company in exile, and her stay reveals how deep his fixation runs.
At a Xindi plant refining weapon-grade kemocite, Archer befriends Gralik, an Arboreal unaware of its purpose, and spares the facility in return for help tracking the shipment.
Parasites rob Archer of new memories, and in a future where the Xindi have destroyed Earth, T'Pol, his caretaker, and Phlox seek a way to erase that timeline.
Enterprise finds a frontier town of humans in the Expanse, descendants of people abducted from 19th-century Earth by the Skagarans, whom they overthrew and keep as an underclass.
To save a comatose Trip, Phlox grows Sim, a fast-aging clone whose neural tissue can heal him, and the crew must reckon with Sim's wish to live.
Sent back to 2004 Detroit by Daniels, Archer and T'Pol hunt three Xindi-Reptilians paying a small-time crook, Loomis, to deliver human blood for a bioweapon.
Zealots who worship the Expanse's spheres as holy seize Enterprise with suicide bombers, intending to turn it against a rival sect, and Archer must outwit their leader, D'Jamat.
Shran's warship turns up in the Expanse offering to help Enterprise find the Xindi test site, but his real orders are to steal the prototype weapon for Andoria.
Having captured weapon designer Degra and erased his recent memories, Archer stages a ruse, posing as his cellmate years later, to learn where the Xindi weapon is built.
Enterprise rescues an alien pilot from a spatial anomaly, Reed and MACO Major Hayes come to blows over their roles, and Trip and T'Pol's neuropressure sessions turn intimate.
While the crew sleeps through a trans-dimensional disturbance, Phlox runs Enterprise alone with only T'Pol for company, until he realizes she is a figment of his strained mind.
Sprayed by a chemical aboard a crashed Xindi-Insectoid ship, Archer becomes obsessed with saving its unhatched eggs, and the crew must mutiny to stop him.
Captured on a one-way mission against the Xindi weapon at Azati Prime, Archer tries to convince Degra that humans are no enemy, while Xindi ships leave Enterprise crippled.
With Enterprise crippled, Archer crosses a moral line and steals a warp coil from Illyrian travelers, while T'Pol confesses her trellium-D addiction to Phlox.
Two Xindi councillors will halt the weapon if Archer proves the Xindi were deceived, as the crew mourns its dead and Trip writes to a fallen crewman's family.
Enterprise meets an aged version of itself, crewed by descendants under Lorian, son of Trip and T'Pol, whose ship was flung back in time by a subspace corridor.
Archer pleads his case before the Xindi Council with proof of the Sphere-Builders' deception, but the Reptilians and Insectoids seize the weapon, Degra is murdered, and Hayes dies.
The Xindi-Reptilians abduct Hoshi to unlock the weapon's launch codes, and Archer joins friendly Xindi factions in a failed bid to stop the weapon from launching toward Earth.
Archer destroys the Xindi weapon en route to Earth, seemingly at the cost of his life, while T'Pol cripples the sphere network; then Archer resurfaces in 1944.
Home at last, the crew scatters to face the Expanse's toll: Archer retreats with Captain Hernandez, Phlox meets human xenophobia, and T'Pol marries Koss on Vulcan.
When genetically engineered Augments seize a Klingon ship, Archer enlists their imprisoned creator, Dr. Arik Soong, to find them, and Soong slips away to rejoin his children.
Soong and his Augments seize Cold Station 12, a medical facility holding frozen Augment embryos and deadly pathogens, and threaten Phlox and its staff to get them.
Malik plots to launch a bioweapon at a Klingon world to ignite war, and when Soong balks, his Augment children turn on him, leaving Archer to stop it.
The bombing of Earth's embassy on Vulcan kills Admiral Forrest, and Archer and T'Pol cross the Forge to find the accused Syrrannites, as Archer receives Surak's katra.
Among the Syrrannites, Archer wrestles with Surak's katra as it guides him to a lost relic, while V'Las orders their enclave bombed and readies a strike on Andoria.
Archer and T'Pol bring the Kir'Shara, Surak's original teachings, before the Vulcan High Command to expose V'Las, while Enterprise wedges itself between Vulcan and Andorian fleets.
Transporter inventor Emory Erickson's experiment aboard Enterprise is secretly a bid to retrieve his son Quinn, lost in subspace years earlier, and it ends in grief.
Two Organians inhabit crew members to observe how Enterprise responds when Hoshi and Trip catch a lethal silicon-based virus, and Archer challenges the watchers to intervene.
Ferrying Tellarite diplomats to talks with Andoria, Enterprise answers Shran's distress call, and the raider that destroyed his ship proves to be a disguised Romulan drone.
Archer builds a joint fleet of humans, Andorians, Tellarites, and Vulcans to trap the Romulan drone, and must survive a ritual duel with Shran to hold it together.
Discovering the Romulan drones are piloted telepathically, Archer and Shran seek out the Aenar, a blind Andorian subspecies, and the Aenar Jhamel helps reach her captive brother.
Phlox is abducted by Klingons desperate to cure a plague born of their Augment experiments, as Trip transfers to Columbia and Section 31 presses Reed into service.
Trip crosses from Columbia at warp to save a sabotaged Enterprise, and Phlox's cure halts the Klingon plague but leaves its victims without their forehead ridges.
Three Orion women gifted to Archer use pheromones to seize control of the ship's men, and only Trip, shielded by his psychic bond with T'Pol, resists.
A ruthless mirror-universe Archer overthrows Captain Forrest to capture the USS Defiant, a Federation ship from another universe's future, adrift in Tholian space.

records.ti: In A Mirror, Darkly, Part II
records.lg: With the ISS Enterprise destroyed, Archer seizes the Defiant and plots to become emperor, crushing T'Pol's revolt, until Hoshi poisons him and takes the throne.
records.ma: In A Mirror, Darkly, Part II (episode)

records.lg: As Earth hosts coalition talks, Trip and T'Pol learn a baby has been engineered from their DNA, a trail leading to John Paxton's xenophobic Terra Prime movement.
Paxton seizes a Martian array and threatens Starfleet Command if non-humans stay in the solar system, while the cloned daughter of Trip and T'Pol sickens and dies.

records.ti: The Girl Who Made the Stars
records.lg: To ease young Michael Burnham's fear of the dark, her father tells the tale of an ancient African girl whose courage brought stars to the night sky.
records.ma: The Girl Who Made the Stars (episode)

records.lg: On Kaminar, young Kelpien Saru rigs a salvaged piece of Ba'ul technology to call out into space, and Lieutenant Philippa Georgiou answers with a way off his world.
A first contact between strangers turns out to be every bit as awkward as a bad first date.
Holodeck hijinks take center stage in a comic short that stacks one hologram upon another.
Trapped in a stalled turbolift on his first day on the Enterprise, Ensign Spock bonds with Number One over questions, Gilbert and Sullivan, and the value of weirdness.
Answering a distress call to Talos IV, Captain Pike is captured by Talosians who trap him in illusions with Vina, a castaway, hoping to breed humans as slaves.
Held by a Tellarite bounty hunter, Harry Mudd schemes to avoid being turned in, but this captive is only one of many android copies of the con man.
New captain Lynne Lucero's first command, the Cabot, is overrun when stubborn scientist Edward Larkin engineers tribbles to multiply as a food source, with fatal results for him.
Guarding a captive Captain Pike during an assault on Starbase 28, Cadet Thira Sidhu must choose between his pleas and her orders, unaware she is being tested.
Sent to investigate an unknown object at the Federation's edge, Shenzhou first officer Michael Burnham encounters T'Kuvma's Klingons and mutinies against Captain Georgiou to strike first.
Klingon ships and Starfleet clash at the binary stars; Georgiou dies trying to capture T'Kuvma, Burnham kills him, and a court sentences her to life for mutiny.
Convict Michael Burnham is brought onto the USS Discovery, whose secretive Captain Lorca recruits her for his spore-drive project after a grim visit to the ravaged USS Glenn.

records.ti: The Butcher's Knife Cares Not for the Lamb's Cry
records.lg: Tasked with studying the Glenn's captured tardigrade, Burnham learns it can steer through the mycelial network, letting Discovery jump in to save the Corvan II colony from Klingons.
records.ma: The Butcher's Knife Cares Not for the Lamb's Cry (episode)

records.lg: Taken prisoner by the Klingons, Lorca escapes alongside Lieutenant Ash Tyler and leaves Harry Mudd behind, while Stamets injects tardigrade DNA to spare the ailing Ripper.
Burnham enters the mind of a bomb-injured Sarek and learns he once picked Spock over her, while Cornwell questions Lorca's fitness and falls into Klingon hands.

records.ti: Magic to Make the Sanest Man Go Mad
records.lg: Harry Mudd traps Discovery in a time loop, plotting to sell the ship to the Klingons, and only Stamets remembers each reset well enough to stop him.
records.ma: Magic to Make the Sanest Man Go Mad (episode)

records.lg: On Pahvo, whose crystal spire could expose cloaked Klingon ships, the planet's peaceful inhabitants enthrall Saru, who sabotages the mission before the Pahvans summon the Klingons themselves.
Defying orders, Lorca keeps Discovery at Pahvo; Stamets' 133 jumps crack the Klingon cloak and doom Kol's flagship, but the last jump sends the ship astray.
Stranded in the mirror universe, the crew poses as their Terran counterparts, Burnham assumes command of the ISS Shenzhou, and an unraveling Tyler kills Dr. Culber.
Ordered to wipe out a rebel base, Burnham tries to spare it, Tyler is unmasked as Voq, and the Terran emperor turns out to be Georgiou.
Aboard the emperor's flagship, Burnham confides her origin to Georgiou and realizes Lorca is Terran, while Stamets meets Culber in the network and L'Rell purges Voq from Tyler.
Lorca seizes the emperor's flagship, whose mycelial reactor is poisoning the network; Burnham sides with Georgiou, Lorca dies, and Discovery escapes home with the emperor, nine months late.

records.ti: The War Without, The War Within
records.lg: Discovery returns to find the Klingons close to winning the war, and a desperate Starfleet secretly installs the mirror Georgiou as captain for a strike on Qo'noS.
records.ma: The War Without, The War Within (episode)

records.lg: Refusing to let Georgiou blow up Qo'noS, Burnham hands the bomb's detonator to L'Rell, who uses the threat to unite the Klingons and end the war.
Captain Pike takes command of Discovery to trace seven red signals, finding the wrecked USS Hiawatha on an asteroid, while Burnham dwells on her estrangement from Spock.
Discovery reaches Terralysium, a pre-warp colony of humans taken from World War III Earth, where Pike weighs General Order 1 and Tilly's curiosity averts disaster.
Hiding aboard the Discovery, the runaway Xahean queen Po finds an unlikely ally in Ensign Tilly, who shares her struggle with the expectations others place on her.
Amanda Grayson brings Spock's psychiatric file aboard, Tilly sees an apparition no one else can, and on Qo'noS L'Rell surrenders her infant son to secure her throne.
A dying alien sphere traps Discovery to upload its memories, Saru survives a Kelpien change he was taught would kill him, and a spore creature cocoons Tilly.
Discovery pushes partway into the mycelial network to rescue Tilly, and Stamets finds Culber alive there, while Section 31 joins the hunt for Spock over Pike's objections.
A signal over Kaminar brings Saru home, where the Ba'ul's long culling of the Kelpiens comes to light and the Red Angel thwarts their attempt at genocide.
On Vulcan, Burnham learns Amanda has been hiding an incoherent Spock, while Pike and Tyler investigate a time rift over Kaminar that lets a future probe infect Airiam.
Burnham brings Spock to Talos IV for healing, where he reveals a vision of galactic annihilation and the siblings confront the rift between them; Pike meets Vina again.
Discovery raids Section 31's headquarters, where Control has killed the admirals, and an infected Airiam turns saboteur until she begs to be ejected into space.
After learning her parents' murder was tied to a Section 31 time-suit project, Burnham risks her life to lure the Red Angel, who proves to be her mother.
Reunited with the mother she thought dead, Burnham learns Gabrielle is fighting Control across time, until Control takes over Leland and Gabrielle is snapped back to the future.
On Boreth, Pike accepts a vision of his own grim fate to win a time crystal, as Burnham and Spock find a Section 31 crew slaughtered by Control.
Unable to destroy Discovery's sphere data, Burnham readies a time suit to lead the ship into the future, and her crew chooses to follow as Control closes in.
Nero, a Romulan from the future, rewrites history by killing Kirk's father and destroying Vulcan, and a young Kirk and Spock, guided by Spock's older self, stop him.
With Klingon and Kelpien help, Enterprise and Discovery hold off Control while Burnham, the true source of the signals, leads Discovery into the future and Spock stays behind.
Pike leaves his Montana retreat to rescue Number One from Kiley 279, a world racing toward warp and civil war, while wrestling with his vision of his fate.
Hunting the terrorist John Harrison to Qo'noS, Kirk learns he is Khan, revived by Admiral Marcus to arm Starfleet for war, then dies, briefly, saving the Enterprise.
An ancient relic on a comet blocks the Enterprise's effort to divert it from an inhabited world, and Uhura must decipher its music while zealots called Shepherds interfere.
An illness that drives victims toward light sweeps the Enterprise, and only Number One stays well, forcing her to confront her hidden identity as a genetically modified Illyrian.
The Gorn ambush a supply run, and security chief La'an Noonien-Singh, who survived their predation as a child, helps Pike outwit them inside a brown dwarf's atmosphere.
A shipboard holiday party takes an unusual turn when a Vulcan is put in charge of providing the entertainment.
A visit from his fiancée T'Pring leaves Spock trapped in her body, and vice versa, just as he and Pike must negotiate with the prickly Rhylkans.

records.ti: Lift Us Where Suffering Cannot Reach
records.lg: Protecting a revered child on the idyllic world Majalis, Pike reunites with his old love Alora, then learns its paradise depends on the boy's suffering inside a machine.
records.ma: Lift Us Where Suffering Cannot Reach (episode)

records.lg: Lured into a trap on a relief mission, the Enterprise is seized by the pirate Captain Angel, who demands the release of Sybok, Spock's estranged brother.
A consciousness in a nebula recasts the crew as figures in the fairy tale Dr. M'Benga reads to his dying daughter, Rukiya, and offers her a new life.
At the wreck of the USS Peregrine on an icy world, the landing party is hunted by Gorn hatchlings, and an infected Hemmer sacrifices himself to save them.
Pike's future self shows him how escaping his fate plays out, a Romulan confrontation that ends in war, and Pike accepts his destiny as Una is arrested.
Answering La'an's distress call, Spock defies orders and takes the Enterprise into disputed space, where the crew uncovers a plot to reignite war with the Klingons.
Facing court-martial for hiding her Illyrian heritage, Una is defended by Neera Ketoul, an estranged childhood friend, who frames her case as a plea for asylum and wins.
Stranded in an altered timeline, La'An and an alternate Kirk hunt a Romulan agent in 2023 Toronto and must save young Khan, her notorious ancestor, to restore history.
Revisiting Rigel VII, Pike's landing party loses memory and identity to the planet's radiation as he confronts Zac Nguyen, a crewman he thought he had lost there.
When aliens mending him after a shuttle crash strip out his Vulcan DNA, a fully human Spock, helped by Chapel, must face a formal dinner with T'Pring's family.
Plagued by a sound only she can hear and the frightening hallucinations it brings, Uhura enlists visiting Lieutenant James Kirk to help hunt down where it comes from.
A time portal drops 24th-century ensigns Boimler and Mariner aboard Pike's Enterprise, where the starstruck pair must be returned home before they disturb the timeline.
Klingon defector Dak'Rah's arrival stirs M'Benga and Chapel's memories of the war on J'Gal, revealing the doctor's secret past as a battlefield killer and ending with Dak'Rah dead.
A failed quantum probability experiment sets the crew singing their secrets, and as the field spreads to other ships, Klingons included, Uhura leads a finale to collapse it.
Answering a Gorn assault on the frontier colony Parnassus Beta, Pike and the Enterprise crew are pulled into open conflict with the reptilian enemy they most dread.
In the wake of the Gorn assault on Parnassus Beta, Pike and his officers are left facing grave, difficult choices as the fight with the invaders continues.
During a Federation celebration, an unexpected and unwelcome visitor intrudes on the quiet reckonings Spock and his crewmates are having with their own lives.
Hunting a cure for the ailing Batel, Pike and M'Benga fly into Klingon territory to the lethal planet Kenfori, where the doctor's war years catch up with him.
Field-testing an experimental holodeck, La'An steps into an invented detective story and takes on a fictional case that has been built for her alone to solve.
A search led by Chapel and Dr. Roger Korby brings the Enterprise to a long-dead civilization's ruins, where something sinister lies hidden.

records.ti: The Sehlat Who Ate Its Tail
records.lg: Lieutenant Commander James Kirk suddenly finds himself commanding the Farragut after a scavenger vessel known as the Destroyer of Worlds overpowers and seizes the Enterprise.
records.ma: The Sehlat Who Ate Its Tail (episode)

records.lg: Helping a planet torn apart by war, Pike and his crew find their every move examined by an inquisitive journalist questioning what Starfleet really stands for.
Turned into Vulcans by a mission gone awry, several Enterprise officers find the real trouble starts when they try to become human again.
Marooned on a poisonous moon, helmsman Erica Ortegas can survive only by acting against the convictions she holds most deeply.
As Pike and Batel ready themselves for her new posting, an old malevolent force resurfaces to menace the Enterprise.
The Enterprise journeys back to the mass extinction 66 million years ago, finding dinosaurs roaming Earth and, on Mars, a civilization on the brink of destruction.
A shuttle team investigating a derelict Federation ship adrift like a ghost encounters phenomena none of them can explain.
A crew vacation on a resort world built for pleasure takes a menacing turn once the planet's promised diversions stop acting like entertainment.
Mistaken for the leader of a resistance movement, Una Chin-Riley is pulled into an occupied world's fight to throw off Klingon rule.
Everyone aboard except Spock becomes a puppet after a transporter mishap, and the crew must repel Orion raiders while learning to work their new bodies.
When disaster hits the Enterprise, separate crises break out across the ship, and scattered teams of crew members each have a single hour to solve theirs.
Trelane recasts Pike's life as an old-fashioned soap opera, and the melodrama becomes an unexpected means for the captain to examine himself.
James Kirk finds his career prospects tangled in Starfleet politics that involve both a powerful admiral and his own father.
An object adrift in space conjures The Kingdom of Elysian, M'Benga's old storybook world, and plunges the crew and their fairy-tale doubles into one shared adventure.
Caught up in a temporal anomaly, Uhura must work alongside an older version of herself to figure out what is causing it.
Lured into a nebula, the Enterprise is shredded by Krall's swarm, and its stranded crew, aided by the scavenger Jaylah, must keep him from attacking Starbase Yorktown.

records.ti: Where No Man Has Gone Before
records.lg: Crossing the barrier at the galaxy's edge, Kirk's old friend Gary Mitchell gains godlike psychic powers and contempt for humans, and Kirk must kill him on Delta Vega.
records.ma: Where No Man Has Gone Before (episode)

records.lg: Rescued con man Harry Mudd brings aboard three women destined as brides for the miners of Rigel XII, whose allure depends on the illegal Venus drug.
Threatened by the colossal ship Fesarius and its commander Balok, Kirk bluffs with a nonexistent substance, corbomite, and learns the menace is a test by a friendly alien.
On planet M-113, a shape-shifting creature that feeds on salt takes the form of McCoy's former love, Nancy Crater, and kills crew members until McCoy shoots it.
Seventeen-year-old Charlie Evans, raised alone by the unseen Thasians, turns his vast mental powers on the crew when he is rejected, until the Thasians return to reclaim him.
A transporter fault splits Kirk into two men, one gentle but indecisive and one savage, while Sulu's landing party freezes on the planet below until the halves rejoin.
Picked up on frozen Psi 2000, an infection dissolves the crew's inhibitions, sending Sulu fencing through corridors and Spock into tears as the ship's orbit decays.
A tardigrade named Ephraim lays her eggs aboard Kirk's Enterprise and spends years dodging a zealous repair droid, DOT-7, before the two unite to save the brood.
After outposts along the Neutral Zone are destroyed, Kirk duels a cloaked Romulan ship and its honorable commander, as the Romulans' resemblance to Vulcans stirs suspicion of Spock.

records.ti: What Are Little Girls Made Of?
records.lg: Nurse Chapel finds her lost fiancé Roger Korby on Exo III, but he plans to seed the galaxy with android duplicates, starting with Kirk, and is one himself.
records.ma: What Are Little Girls Made Of? (episode)

records.lg: A longevity experiment has killed every adult on an Earth-duplicate planet, and when the landing party catches the disease, McCoy races for a cure among centuries-old children.
At the Tantalus V penal colony, Kirk and Dr. Helen Noel find Dr. Tristan Adams's celebrated neural neutralizer empties and reshapes minds, as Spock mind-melds with a victim.
Kirk suspects touring actor Anton Karidian is Kodos the Executioner, who slaughtered thousands on Tarsus IV, as the surviving witnesses, Kirk among them, are targeted one by one.
Spock hijacks the Enterprise with the crippled Christopher Pike aboard, locking its heading for forbidden Talos IV, and faces a court-martial that replays Pike's first visit there.
Spock's court-martial plays out through Talosian images of Pike's captivity, and the true purpose emerges: to give the crippled Pike an illusory life on Talos IV with Vina.
On an idyllic shore-leave planet, the crew's passing thoughts take solid form, from a white rabbit to Kirk's old Academy tormentor, in an amusement park built by aliens.
When the shuttle Galileo crashes on Taurus II, Spock's first command falters as giant creatures pick off his crew, until a desperate fuel flare catches the Enterprise's eye.
The Enterprise is held captive by Trelane, a playful, all-powerful being with a taste for Earth's past glories, until his unseen parents call him away.
After the Gorn destroy the Cestus III outpost, the Metrons pit Kirk against the Gorn captain in single combat, and Kirk builds a crude cannon but chooses mercy.
Flung back to 1969 by a black star, the Enterprise beams aboard Air Force pilot John Christopher, then must return him and erase every trace of its visit.
Kirk stands trial for the death of officer Ben Finney, damned by computer records, until Spock proves they were doctored by Finney himself, alive and hiding aboard.
On Beta III, a docile population broken only by the violent Red Hour obeys the unseen Landru, a centuries-old computer that Kirk talks into destroying itself.
Revived from the sleeper ship Botany Bay, Khan Noonien Singh and his engineered supermen seize the Enterprise, and Kirk, after retaking it, exiles them to Ceti Alpha V.
Eminiar VII fights Vendikar by computer simulation, with the listed dead reporting to disintegration chambers, and when the Enterprise is counted among them, Kirk smashes the war computers.
On Omicron Ceti III, spores that bring perfect contentment seduce the crew and even Spock, who finds love with Leila Kalomi, until Kirk discovers anger breaks their hold.
A creature killing miners on Janus VI turns out, through Spock's mind-meld, to be the Horta, a mother defending the eggs the miners have been unknowingly destroying.
On Organia, Kirk and Spock urge its placid people to resist Kor's Klingon occupiers, then learn the Organians are energy beings who end the war themselves.
A rift between universes brings Lazarus, a man locked in endless war with his antimatter double, and Kirk must trap them both between realities to avert total annihilation.
A dangerous Klingon assault becomes even harder to handle when the crew gets tangled up in an unfortunate choice of words.

records.ti: The City on the Edge of Forever
records.lg: An overdosed McCoy alters history through the Guardian of Forever, and Kirk, pursuing him into 1930 New York, falls for Edith Keeler, whose death he must allow.
records.ma: The City on the Edge of Forever (episode)

records.lg: Flying parasites drive the colonists of Deneva mad, killing Kirk's brother Sam, and after Spock is infected, the crew learns intense light can destroy the creatures.
Gripped by pon farr, Spock must return to Vulcan to marry T'Pring, who invokes a ritual challenge that forces Kirk to fight his friend to the death.
The being once worshipped on Earth as Apollo grips the Enterprise with a giant energy hand, demands the crew's devotion, and courts Lieutenant Carolyn Palamas as his queen.
The ancient Earth probe Nomad, merged with an alien sterilizer, mistakes Kirk for its creator and purges imperfection, until Kirk talks it into destroying itself for its errors.
Swept into a mirror universe by a transporter accident, Kirk, Uhura, McCoy, and Scott must pass as officers of a ruthless empire, aided by a bearded, calculating Spock.
The ageless natives of lush Gamma Trianguli VI serve the machine god Vaal, which attacks the landing party, and Kirk frees the people by destroying it.
Commodore Matt Decker, sole survivor of the Constellation, commandeers the Enterprise to avenge his crew on a planet-killing machine, and Kirk destroys it with Decker's wrecked ship.
On Pyris VII, the alien explorers Korob and Sylvia greet the landing party with witches, a haunted castle, and a black cat, illusions drawn from humanity's darkest fears.
Kirk's shuttle is drawn to an asteroid where Zefram Cochrane, the long-vanished inventor of warp drive, lives kept young by the Companion, an energy being who loves him.
Ferrying delegates to Babel, the Enterprise carries Spock's estranged father Sarek, suspected of murder and dying, and Spock must choose between command and giving blood to save him.
Negotiating for mining rights on Capella IV against a Klingon rival, Kirk, Spock, and McCoy end up protecting Eleen, the pregnant widow of the planet's murdered ruler.
Radiation on Gamma Hydra IV ages Kirk, Scott, McCoy, and Spock decades in days, and the key to a cure lies with Chekov, the one officer spared.
Accused of murdering women on Argelius II, Scotty is cleared when the killer proves to be Redjac, a fear-feeding entity that once stalked London as Jack the Ripper.
An android named Norman hijacks the Enterprise to a planet of androids ruled in name by Harry Mudd, and the crew escapes by overloading the machines with illogic.
Kirk becomes fixated on killing a vampiric cloud creature that ravaged the Farragut's crew years ago, and hunts it with Ensign Garrovick, son of the captain it killed.
Guarding grain at Space Station K-7, Kirk contends with a pompous official, brawling Klingons, and fast-breeding tribbles, which end up exposing poisoned grain and a Klingon spy.
Snatched away to Triskelion, Kirk, Uhura, and Chekov become trained gladiators for the Providers, disembodied brains who bet on them, until Kirk wagers everyone's freedom.
The Iotians have modeled their entire society on a book about 1920s Chicago mobs left by an earlier ship, so Kirk plays gangster to unite the rival bosses.
Once Spock senses the death of the Vulcan-crewed Intrepid, the Enterprise finds a giant energy-eating amoeba about to reproduce, and Spock pilots a shuttle into it.
Finding Klingons arming one faction of a peaceful people on Neural, Kirk grimly decides to supply matching weapons to protect his friend Tyree's tribe.
Sargon and two fellow survivors of an ancient race borrow Kirk, Spock, and Dr. Ann Mulhall's bodies to build android forms, until Henoch refuses to give Spock's back.
Searching for historian John Gill on Ekos, Kirk and Spock find he has modeled the planet on Nazi Germany, and his regime is now persecuting the neighboring Zeons.
Kelvans from Andromeda seize the Enterprise and shrink most of the crew into blocks, leaving Kirk and three officers to turn the invaders' borrowed human senses against them.
The Exeter's crew lies dead of a plague, and on Omega IV Kirk finds its captain, Ron Tracey, arming the Kohms against the Yangs in search of immortality.
Richard Daystrom's M-5 computer is installed to run the Enterprise, then turns war games into real attacks on Starfleet ships until Kirk convinces it it has committed murder.
On a planet where Rome never fell, Captain Merik of the lost Beagle, now an imperial officer, sends Kirk, Spock, and McCoy toward death in televised gladiator games.
Kara, leader of a planet's cave-dwelling women, steals Spock's brain to run their underground machinery, and McCoy, boosted by an alien teaching device, must put it back.
Feigning instability, Kirk crosses into Romulan territory as cover for a secret mission: while Spock distracts the Romulan commander, a disguised Kirk steals her cloaking device.
Stripped of his memory, Kirk lives as Kirok among transplanted Native Americans and marries Miramanee, while Spock races to stop an asteroid from striking their planet.
Orphaned children from the Triacus colony, under the sway of the malevolent Gorgan, take over the Enterprise, until Kirk breaks the spell by making them face their grief.

records.ti: Is There in Truth No Beauty?
records.lg: Blind telepath Dr. Miranda Jones escorts Kollos, a Medusan ambassador whose appearance drives humans mad, and her jealousy of Spock nearly costs him his mind.
records.ma: Is There in Truth No Beauty? (episode)

records.lg: Cast by the Melkotians as the doomed Clanton gang, Kirk and four officers must relive the O.K. Corral shootout until a mind-meld convinces them the bullets are unreal.
An energy being that feeds on hatred traps the crew and Kang's Klingons in endless sword-fighting, until both sides refuse to fight and laugh it off the ship.

records.ti: For the World is Hollow and I Have Touched the Sky
records.lg: Dying of an incurable illness, McCoy falls for Natira, priestess of Yonada, an asteroid ship whose unwitting people are headed for impact with a populated planet.
records.ma: For the World is Hollow and I Have Touched the Sky (episode)

records.lg: Kirk vanishes into interspace with the derelict Defiant, and as the Tholians spin an energy web around the Enterprise, Spock and McCoy clash while trying to retrieve him.
Psychokinetic followers of Plato force Kirk, Spock, Uhura, and Chapel to perform humiliating spectacles, until McCoy traces their powers to kironide and the crew gains them too.
Hyperaccelerated Scalosians, moving too fast to be seen, seize the Enterprise to breed with its crew, and their queen Deela speeds Kirk up to be her mate.
The Vians torture Kirk, Spock, and McCoy as the Minara sun nears nova, testing whether Gem, a mute empath, will risk her life to heal them.
Escorting the imperious Elaan of Elas to wed the ruler of rival Troyius, Kirk falls under the spell of her tears as a Klingon ship stalks them.
At the Elba II asylum, shape-shifting former hero Garth of Izar takes over and holds Kirk and Spock captive, scheming to seize the Enterprise and conquer the galaxy.

records.ti: Let That Be Your Last Battlefield
records.lg: Two Cherons, Lokai and his pursuer Bele, drag the Enterprise into their feud over which side of their faces is black, even after learning their world is dead.
records.ma: Let That Be Your Last Battlefield (episode)

records.lg: Beamed onto an empty replica of the Enterprise, Kirk meets Odona, whose overcrowded world Gideon wants the disease in his blood to thin its population.
Stranded on a planet built by the vanished Kalandans, Kirk's landing party is hunted by a lethal computer projection of Losira, the outpost's long-dead commander.
At the galaxy's center, the Enterprise enters Megas-Tu, a realm where magic works, and Kirk must defend the kindly Lucien in a Salem-style trial before its wary inhabitants.
Energy beings from Zetar, last remnants of a dead people, ravage the Memory Alpha library planetoid and try to possess Lieutenant Mira Romaine, the woman Scotty loves.
Ferrying a Slaver stasis box aboard the shuttle Copernicus, Spock, Uhura, and Sulu are hijacked by Kzinti who covet the ancient, shape-shifting weapon inside.
Harry Mudd peddles a love crystal he believes is a sham, but when Chapel uses it on Spock, the charm proves real, with volatile consequences.
Needing zenite to stop a plague, Kirk finds the cloud city Stratos oppressing the Troglyte miners below, whose supposed inferiority comes from the mineral's toxic gas.
The rescue of long-missing philanthropist Carter Winston delights his fiancée aboard the Enterprise, until he proves to be a shape-shifting Vendorian spy working with Romulans.
Drawn to a dead star, the Enterprise finds an ancient alien derelict imprisoning a malevolent energy being, which escapes into the ship and must be tricked into leaving.
Stranded in the Delta Triangle with Kor's Klingon cruiser, the Enterprise finds Elysia, a timeless society of lost ships, and must cooperate with the Klingons to break free.
Dropouts who reject technology, led by the fanatical Dr. Sevrin, hijack the Enterprise to reach the legendary planet Eden, which proves beautiful but lethally poisonous.

records.ti: One of Our Planets Is Missing
records.lg: A vast living cloud devouring whole worlds heads for the populated planet Mantilles, and Spock must mind-meld with it to persuade it to turn away.
records.ma: One of Our Planets Is Missing (episode)

records.lg: Erased from history after a Guardian of Forever mission, Spock poses as cousin Selek on Vulcan to save his boyhood self, though his pet sehlat I-Chaya dies.
Seeking a plague cure, Kirk meets Flint, an immortal who once lived as da Vinci and Brahms, and falls for Rayna, the android Flint built as his companion.
Rescued from a Klingon pursuit, Cyrano Jones brings aboard supposedly non-breeding tribbles that instead grow enormous, while Koloth hunts for a stolen tribble predator.
Lured by a siren call, Kirk and his male officers begin aging to death under the spell of life-draining women, until Uhura takes command and leads a rescue.
Rock-like Excalbians stage a battle of good against evil, pitting Kirk, Spock, Abraham Lincoln, and Surak against re-creations of Kahless, Genghis Khan, and other infamous villains.
On the water world Argo, a sea monster's attack leaves Kirk and Spock able to breathe only underwater, and they must win help from a wary undersea civilization.
Searching Lactra VII for a missing survey crew, Kirk, Spock, and McCoy are caught by giant telepathic slugs and held as exhibits in their zoo.
On Phylos, sentient plant beings and Keniclius 5, a cloned Eugenics Wars scientist, abduct Spock to grow a giant copy of him to enforce peace across the galaxy.
Kirk's former lover Janice Lester swaps bodies with him to take the Enterprise, and only Spock, after a mind-meld, believes the real captain is trapped in her body.
A burst of strange radiation shrinks the Enterprise crew to miniature size, the doing of the tiny Terratins, who need help escaping their unstable world.
Back on the shore-leave planet, the crew learns its Keeper is dead and the master computer, tired of serving, is turning the park's fantasies deadly and abducting Uhura.
Through a time portal on doomed Sarpeidon, Kirk lands in a witch-hunting past while Spock and McCoy reach an ice age, where Spock falls for the exile Zarabeth.
Sent by the Vedala to retrieve the Soul of the Skorr before its theft sparks a holy war, Kirk and Spock discover the thief is on their team.
After the ship crosses a strange energy cloud, the Enterprise's computer develops a taste for pranks that escalate from harmless gags to trapping officers in the recreation room.
Arrested on Dramia for a plague that ravaged a colony nineteen years earlier, McCoy must clear himself as the same disease spreads through the Enterprise.

records.ti: How Sharper Than a Serpent's Tooth
records.lg: A winged serpent being who visited ancient Earth as Kukulkan traps the Enterprise, demanding the reverence humans once gave him, until Kirk convinces him they have outgrown him.
records.ma: How Sharper Than a Serpent's Tooth (episode)

records.lg: When Orion raiders hijack the freighter carrying the drug Spock needs to survive, Kirk must wrest it from pirates who would rather die than be caught.
Carrying Commodore Robert April, its first captain, the Enterprise falls into a universe where time runs backward, and April must command as the crew regresses into children.
Honorary commander Ari bn Bem of Pandro, a being who can split into separate parts, secretly tests the crew to judge whether the Federation is fit for contact.
Admiral Kirk reclaims the newly refitted Enterprise to intercept a vast cloud bound for Earth, at whose core lies V'Ger, an old NASA Voyager probe seeking its creator.

records.ti: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
records.lg: Marooned for fifteen years, Khan seizes the starship Reliant and the Genesis device to take revenge on Kirk, and victory in the Mutara Nebula costs Spock his life.
records.ma: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

records.ti: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
records.lg: Learning McCoy carries Spock's spirit, Kirk steals the Enterprise for Genesis, losing his son and his ship to the Klingon Kruge before Spock is restored on Vulcan.
records.ma: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock

records.ti: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
records.lg: An alien probe ravages Earth while calling to extinct humpback whales, so Kirk's crew takes a captured Klingon ship back to 1986 San Francisco to bring two home.
records.ma: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home

records.ti: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
records.lg: Spock's half-brother Sybok takes hostages on Nimbus III to lure the Enterprise-A, then commandeers it to cross the Great Barrier in search of God at the galaxy's center.
records.ma: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier

records.ti: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
records.lg: After the moon Praxis explodes, the Klingons seek peace, but Chancellor Gorkon's assassination lands Kirk and McCoy on Rura Penthe while conspirators on both sides scheme against peace.
records.ma: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

records.lg: Recruited by Section 31, Starfleet's secret division, former Terran emperor Philippa Georgiou falls in with a team of misfits to recover a doomsday weapon from her bloody past.
On the Enterprise-D's first mission, Q puts humanity on trial, and Picard's new crew must prove itself by uncovering that Farpoint Station is a captive shape-shifting space creature.
A contagion from the research ship Tsiolkovsky, the same intoxicant that once swept Kirk's Enterprise, loosens the Enterprise-D crew's inhibitions just as a collapsing star threatens the ship.
Lutan, ruler of Ligon II, abducts Tasha Yar to make her his wife, jeopardizing a vaccine the Enterprise needs and forcing Yar to duel his current wife.
On Omicron Theta, the crew assembles Data's android brother, Lore, who betrayed the colony to the Crystalline Entity and now impersonates Data to feed it the Enterprise.
While the Enterprise ferries feuding Antican and Selay delegates, an energy being picked up from a passing cloud jumps between crew members and ends up possessing Picard.
On the pleasure-loving Edo world, Wesley Crusher is sentenced to death for trampling a flower bed, and Picard must weigh the Prime Directive against the boy's life.

records.ti: Where No One Has Gone Before
records.lg: Warp tests by the arrogant engineer Kosinski fling the Enterprise to a realm where thought becomes reality, and only his alien assistant, the Traveler, can guide it home.
records.ma: Where No One Has Gone Before (episode)

records.lg: Troi's long-arranged marriage to Wyatt Miller brings Lwaxana aboard, but Wyatt's heart belongs to a woman from his dreams, who is aboard a Tarellian plague ship nearing Haven.
Secretly taking a lethal youth drug, aging Admiral Mark Jameson handles a hostage crisis on Mordan IV staged by Karnas, who wants revenge for the war Jameson fueled.
While the Bynars upgrade the Enterprise's computers, Riker is captivated by Minuet, a holodeck woman they designed, as they hijack the ship to save their homeworld.
Chasing Ferengi thieves, the Enterprise gets caught with them in the power-draining grip of an ancient Tkon Empire outpost, whose guardian, Portal, puts Riker to the test.
Wesley competes for a place at Starfleet Academy in testing on Relva VII and loses to a Benzite, while Admiral Quinn's investigator Remmick scrutinizes Picard's command.
At a terraforming station on Velara III, the Enterprise discovers that the tiny crystalline lifeforms in the planet's soil are intelligent and are fighting back against the project.
Klingon renegades rescued from a wrecked freighter urge Worf to join their quest for glory, and he proves his loyalty to Starfleet by killing their leader, Korris.
The sterile people of the legendary hidden world Aldea kidnap the Enterprise's children, and Wesley organizes the young captives' resistance while Picard negotiates for their return.
Q hands Riker godlike power to lure him into the Q, but when his friends turn down the gifts he offers, including sight for Geordi, Riker renounces it.
Trying to rescue Troi from a downed shuttle on Vagra II, the away team meets Armus, a spiteful tar-like being who kills Tasha Yar on a whim.
Searching the matriarchal planet Angel One for survivors of a lost freighter, Riker finds them wanted as subversives, while a fast-spreading virus leaves the Enterprise short-handed.
Paul Manheim's time experiments send loops rippling through the Enterprise, and Picard must face Manheim's wife Jenice, the woman he once left waiting in Paris.
The Ornarans' supposed plague cure, felicium, proves to be a narcotic sold by the Brekkians, and Picard undercuts the trade by refusing to repair their freighters.
Seeking revenge for his son, Ferengi DaiMon Bok gives Picard his old ship, the Stargazer, and uses a mind-altering device to make him relive the Battle of Maxia.
Warned by his friend Walker Keel, Picard returns to Earth and finds Starfleet's top brass controlled by parasitic aliens, whose leader lives inside Commander Remmick.
On Minos, whose arms dealers died by their own product, an automated weapons demo stalks the away team while Geordi commands the ship against it in orbit.
As three revived 20th-century humans adjust to the future, the Enterprise investigates destroyed outposts along the Neutral Zone and faces the Romulans after decades of silence.
A Jarada scan damages the holodeck while Picard plays detective Dixon Hill, trapping him in 1941 San Francisco with lethal gangsters just before he must greet the Jarada.
An alien presence impregnates Troi with a fast-growing son, Ian, who gives up his life to save the ship, while Wesley, choosing to stay aboard, meets Guinan.
Holding the Enterprise in a starless void, the being Nagilum means to kill much of the crew to learn about death, and Picard arms the self-destruct in defiance.
When Geordi asks the holodeck for a foe who can outwit Data, it creates a self-aware Professor Moriarty, who kidnaps Dr. Pulaski and seizes control of the ship.
Rescuing the charming rogue Thadiun Okona embroils the Enterprise in a dispute between two worlds over a stolen jewel and a pregnancy, while Data studies comedy.
Dying genius Ira Graves, who calls himself Data's grandfather, secretly transfers his mind into Data's body, and the android starts behaving like a jealous, arrogant stranger.
Deaf mediator Riva, who speaks through a telepathic chorus, loses his interpreters to a gunman's attack and must find another way to broker peace on Solais V.
The Lantree's crew all died of rapid aging, traced to engineered children at the Darwin station, and when Pulaski is infected, only the transporter can restore her.
On an officer exchange aboard the Klingon ship Pagh, Riker must outwit Captain Kargan, who blames the Enterprise for a hull-eating bacterium and readies an attack.
When cyberneticist Bruce Maddox moves to dismantle Data, Picard wins the android the right to refuse at a hearing where Riker is forced to argue against him.
Wesley falls for Salia, the young ruler being taken home to unite war-torn Daled IV, only to learn she and her fierce guardian Anya are shape-shifters.
Iconian software that destroyed the Yamato spreads to the Enterprise and to a nearby Romulan warship, and Picard must search Iconia's ruins for a way to purge it.
Riker, Worf, and Data are trapped in a casino hotel that aliens copied from a pulp novel for a lost 21st-century astronaut, until they play out its plot.
A shuttle turns up carrying a dazed second Picard, displaced six hours from the future, and the captain must break the cycle that ends with his ship destroyed.
Offered command of the Aries, Riker confronts years of resentment toward his father Kyle before turning the post down, while Worf's friends stage a painful Klingon rite.
Data befriends Sarjenka, a child on the collapsing world Drema IV, by radio, and after a Prime Directive debate the crew saves her planet and wipes her memory.
To prove humanity isn't ready for what lies ahead, Q flings the Enterprise 7,000 light-years into the path of the Borg, and Picard must ask him for help.
Picard confides the story of his artificial heart to Wesley while traveling for risky surgery, as the dim-seeming Pakleds kidnap Geordi to extract Federation technology.
Rescuing Bringloidi farmers from solar flares, the Enterprise finds their sister colony of Mariposan clones degrading, and Picard brokers a merger of the two groups.
Going through the Betazoid Phase, Lwaxana Troi hunts for a husband and fixes on Picard, who hides in the holodeck, until she exposes two Antedean delegates as assassins.
Half-Klingon envoy K'Ehleyr, Worf's former lover, helps him face down the T'Ong, a sleeper ship whose crew wakes believing the war never ended, by posing as its commanders.
Refereed by the Zakdorn strategist Kolrami, a war game pits Riker in the aged Hathaway against Picard's Enterprise, until a Ferengi attack forces a desperate bluff.
Stung by an alien vine on Surata IV, Riker lies near death as Pulaski drives the infection back by forcing him to relive his most painful memories.
Wesley's escaped nanites evolve into a thinking colony inside the ship's computer, endangering the Enterprise and Dr. Paul Stubbs's long-awaited stellar experiment, until Data brokers a truce.
Data must persuade 15,000 stubborn colonists on Tau Cygna V to evacuate while Picard stalls the Sheliak, who own the planet by treaty and will exterminate them.
An elderly couple are the only survivors on devastated Rana IV, and Picard learns the husband, Kevin Uxbridge, is a godlike Douwd who erased a species in grief.
When proto-Vulcan Mintakans glimpse a hidden observation post, they start worshipping Picard, who must prove he is mortal, even taking an arrow to do so.
After archaeologist Marla Aster dies on Worf's away mission, an alien re-creates her for her orphaned son Jeremy, and Worf offers the boy a Klingon bond of kinship.
With the Enterprise snared by the ancient trap that doomed a Promellian cruiser, Geordi conjures a holodeck version of engine designer Leah Brahms to find a way out.
Stranded on stormy Galorndon Core, a blinded Geordi must team up with a Romulan soldier, while Worf refuses the transfusion that could save another Romulan aboard.
Troi falls for Devinoni Ral, a negotiator secretly using Betazoid empathy to win rights to the Barzan wormhole, which proves far less stable than advertised.
Talks between Acamar and its raiding Gatherer clans are threatened by Yuta, a secret assassin avenging a feud, and Riker, who has fallen for her, must shoot her.
Admiral Jarok defects from the Romulans to warn of a base at Nelvana III, but his superiors fed him false intelligence to lure the Enterprise into a trap.
Reviewing Angosia III's bid for Federation membership, the crew captures escaped prisoner Roga Danar and learns he is an engineered super-soldier his government imprisoned after its war.
On Rutia IV, separatist leader Kyril Finn abducts Dr. Crusher to drag the Federation into his people's armed struggle, and Picard soon becomes his hostage too.
Expelled by the Continuum and made human, Q seeks shelter on the Enterprise, where a selfless act against the vengeful Calamarain wins his powers back.
Accused of killing scientist Nel Apgar on Tanuga IV, Riker faces holodeck re-creations of conflicting testimony until the crew proves Apgar died trying to kill him.
The Enterprise-C's leap forward in time rewrites history into a losing Klingon war, and Guinan persuades Picard to send it, with Tasha Yar aboard, back to die.
Data builds an android daughter, Lal, and resists an admiral's order to take her away for study, until her rapidly developing mind suffers a fatal cascade failure.
Worf discovers a brother, Kurn, and returns to the Klingon homeworld to fight charges that their father betrayed Khitomer, ultimately accepting disgrace to prevent civil war.
Aliens studying leadership imprison Picard with three strangers and put a duplicate in his place, whose erratic orders and advances toward Crusher soon unsettle the crew.
Picard's vacation on Risa is upended by Vash, a scheming archaeologist, as a Ferengi and two time-traveling Vorgons chase the Tox Uthat, a weapon from the 27th century.
Racing the Romulans to a living ship called Tin Man, the Enterprise relies on Tam Elbrun, a Betazoid telepath who finds in the lonely being a kindred spirit.
Shy engineer Reginald Barclay retreats into holodeck fantasies starring caricatures of his crewmates, until he helps track down the contamination causing the ship's malfunctions.
Staging Data's death in a shuttle blast, collector Kivas Fajo keeps the android as a trophy, and Fajo's cruelty pushes Data to the brink of killing him.
Aging Ambassador Sarek comes aboard to seal a treaty with the Legarans, but his Bendii Syndrome floods the crew with violent emotions until Picard melds minds with him.
Smitten Ferengi DaiMon Tog abducts Lwaxana Troi, Deanna, and Riker to exploit Lwaxana's telepathy, and Picard wins her back by playing a jealous lover spouting Shakespeare.
Nursed to health aboard the Enterprise, an amnesiac Zalkonian known as John Doe is hunted by his own people as he evolves into a being of pure energy.
Years ahead of Starfleet's estimates, the Borg invade, abducting Picard and remaking him as Locutus, which leaves Riker to order fire on the cube holding his captain.

records.ti: The Best of Both Worlds, Part II
records.lg: The Borg, guided by Locutus, annihilate the fleet at Wolf 359, and Riker must retrieve Picard so Data can reach through him to put the cube to sleep.
records.ma: The Best of Both Worlds, Part II (episode)

records.lg: Still recovering from assimilation, Picard returns to his family's vineyard in France and breaks down with his brother Robert, while Worf's adoptive human parents visit the Enterprise.
Called home by Noonien Soong's homing signal, Data hijacks the Enterprise despite a gravely ill boy aboard, and Lore steals the emotion chip Soong made for Data.
Picard takes in Jono, a human teen raised by the Talarian captain whose forces killed his parents, and after the boy stabs him, sends him back to Endar.
After Wesley's warp bubble experiment misfires, Dr. Crusher watches crewmates vanish unnoticed by anyone else, until Wesley and the Traveler reach her shrinking pocket universe.
To rescue a freighter crew held hostage by a faction on Turkana IV, the Enterprise enlists Tasha Yar's sister Ishara, whose friendship with Data hides her own agenda.
Named Arbiter of Succession by the dying K'mpec, Picard must choose between Duras and Gowron, while Worf meets his son Alexander and kills Duras for murdering K'Ehleyr.
About to leave for Starfleet Academy, Wesley must keep a gravely hurt Picard alive after a mining shuttle goes down on a barren moon.
Robbed of her empathic sense, Troi turns bitter and tries to resign, as two-dimensional lifeforms drag the Enterprise toward a lethal cosmic string.
Data chronicles a day for Bruce Maddox, from learning to dance for O'Brien and Keiko's wedding to exposing a Vulcan ambassador's transporter death as a Romulan spy's escape.
Convinced the Cardassians are secretly rearming, Captain Benjamin Maxwell of the Phoenix begins destroying their ships, and O'Brien, once his crewman, must help talk him down.
Con artist Ardra poses as the devil of Ventaxian legend, come to collect on a thousand-year-old contract, and Picard exposes her trickery in an arbitration judged by Data.
After an apparent wormhole leaves the crew missing a day, Data's evasions arouse suspicion, until Picard learns he ordered Data to hide an encounter with the reclusive Paxans.
Surgically disguised as a Malcorian, Riker is hurt and exposed on the eve of their first warp flight, and Picard must reveal the Federation to a wary chancellor.
Geordi meets the real Leah Brahms, married and offended by his holodeck copy of her, as they try to wean an orphaned space creature feeding off the Enterprise.
Trapped in Tyken's Rift, the crew can't dream and slides into paranoia, while Troi's recurring nightmare proves to be a plea from aliens stuck there too.
Riker wakes sixteen years on as captain, with a son he can't remember, in a future that proves to be a fantasy spun by a lonely alien child.
Members of an old Tarchannen III away team, including Geordi and his friend Susanna Leijten, are drawn back to that world as an alien parasite transforms them.
An alien probe turns Barclay into a genius who wires his mind into the computer and flings the Enterprise to the galaxy's center, where the Cytherians await.
Noticing Picard's awkward reunion with Vash, Q casts him as Robin Hood and her as Maid Marian, with the senior staff as reluctant Merry Men.
Retired Admiral Norah Satie's hunt for a saboteur swells into a witch-hunt that targets a part-Romulan crewman, Simon Tarses, and finally Picard himself.
Lwaxana falls for Timicin, a Kaelon scientist trying to save his people's dying sun, and fights his decision to honor the custom requiring him to die at sixty.
Dr. Crusher falls for Ambassador Odan, then learns he is a Trill symbiont, which Riker must carry to finish the peace talks until a new host arrives.
Seized on the way to Risa, Geordi is programmed by Romulans to kill a Klingon governor, and Data must expose the plot and the Klingon envoy abetting it.
Data attempts romance with Lieutenant Jenna D'Sora by writing a subroutine for it, while a dark-matter nebula causes objects and people to phase out around the ship.
Gowron's accession sparks a Klingon civil war, and Worf resigns from Starfleet to fight beside Kurn, while a Romulan with Tasha Yar's face backs the Duras family.
Picard forms a tachyon blockade to expose Romulan aid to the Duras forces, Data takes command of the Sutherland, and Sela reveals herself as Tasha Yar's daughter.
Stranding himself with Picard on El-Adrel IV, the Tamarian captain Dathon teaches him a language built on myth, dying of a beast's wounds just as they connect.
Picard reluctantly takes on disgraced Bajoran officer Ro Laren to find the rebel Orta, and she uncovers an admiral's secret deal with Cardassia behind the mission.
Xenologist Kila Marr, whose son died at Omicron Theta, joins the hunt for the Crystalline Entity, distrusts Data, and destroys the creature just as communication seems possible.
A quantum filament cripples the Enterprise, leaving Troi in command of the bridge, Picard stuck in a turbolift with three children, and Worf delivering Keiko O'Brien's baby.
A headset game Riker brings home from Risa enslaves the crew for a Ktarian takeover, leaving a visiting Wesley and Ensign Robin Lefler to fight it.
When Ambassador Spock turns up on Romulus, Picard visits the dying Sarek, then sets off with Data, disguised as Romulans, on a borrowed Klingon ship to find him.
Found on Romulus pursuing reunification with Vulcan, Spock joins Picard and Data to foil Sela's plan to turn his mission into cover for an invasion of Vulcan.
Self-proclaimed 26th-century historian Berlinghoff Rasmussen watches the crew fight to save Penthara IV from an asteroid winter, but he is a 22nd-century thief with a stolen time pod.
Worf struggles to raise his son Alexander, newly arrived to live aboard, while a test of soliton-wave propulsion runs out of control and endangers a colony.
Timothy, a boy orphaned when the research ship Vico was destroyed, copes by imitating Data, as the crew learns the Black Cluster, not the boy, wrecked the vessel.
Ullian telepaths come aboard to collect memories, and Troi, Riker, and Crusher fall into comas after violent recollections, until one researcher, Jev, is exposed as their assailant.
Saving Moab IV's genetically engineered colony from a stellar fragment requires technology inspired by Geordi's VISOR, and the rescue fractures the perfect society as colonists choose to leave.
Their memories wiped, the crew follows planted orders to attack the Lysians under a first officer, MacDuff, who is actually a Satarran using them as a weapon.
Posing as the ghosts of a lost starship's crew, alien convicts possess Data, Troi, and O'Brien and seize hostages in Ten Forward to free their fellow prisoners.
Paralyzed by a falling container, Worf plans ritual suicide, and his only alternative is a risky, untested procedure from Dr. Toby Russell, whose methods appall Crusher.
Riker falls for Soren, one of the genderless J'naii, who secretly identifies as female, but her society seizes her and forces her through psychological reprogramming.
Caught in a loop that always ends with the ship exploding after hitting the Bozeman, the crew breaks free only when Data sends himself a clue.
After a banned maneuver kills a Nova Squadron cadet, Wesley joins his squad leader Nick Locarno in covering it up, until Picard pushes him to tell the truth.
Aboard for an arranged wedding to a rigid Kostolain minister, Lwaxana Troi coaxes Alexander into defying Worf's rules, as metal-eating parasites chew through the ship.
Hosting peace talks, Picard must guard Kamala, an empathic metamorph who becomes whatever her companion desires, and resist their mutual attraction as she goes to her arranged marriage.
Exploring a nebula, the Enterprise picks up an alien that takes the form of young Clara Sutter's imaginary friend Isabella and turns hostile over how adults treat children.
Picard plans to turn a rescued Borg youth into a weapon against the Collective, until Geordi's friendship makes the drone an individual named Hugh whom Picard cannot sacrifice.
Declared dead after a transporter mishap, Geordi and Ro are really phased and invisible, and must find a way to warn the crew of a Romulan sabotage plan.
An alien probe gives Picard a whole lifetime in minutes as Kamin, a husband and father on the doomed world Kataan, so its vanished people will be remembered.
Data's five-century-old severed head turns up beneath San Francisco, and the mystery sends him back to 1893, where he meets Guinan, with the crew soon following.
Posing as actors in 1893 San Francisco, the away team, dogged by a suspicious Samuel Clemens, stops the Devidians from preying on cholera victims and brings Data home.
Forced to overcome his terror of transporters, Barclay spots creatures in the beam and discovers they are the missing crew of the Yosemite, trapped in the matter stream.
Ambassador Alkar secretly dumps his dark emotions into Troi to keep his mind clear for peace talks, leaving her erratic and rapidly aging until Crusher fakes her death.
Rescued from a transporter buffer after 75 years aboard a ship wrecked on a Dyson sphere, Montgomery Scott feels obsolete until he and Geordi must save the Enterprise.
Riker and other crew members wake exhausted each morning, and a holodeck reconstruction reveals they are being abducted in their sleep by aliens from a subspace realm.
Q arrives to evaluate Amanda Rogers, an intern unaware she is a Q, who learns the Continuum killed her parents for living as humans and finally joins it.
A transporter accident turns Picard, Ro, Guinan, and Keiko into twelve-year-olds with adult minds, and when Ferengi seize the Enterprise, the children lead the fight to retake it.
An experiment linking Data to the computer glitches a holodeck Western, and Worf, Alexander, and Troi must survive outlaws who share Data's looks and strength.
Data suspects the exocomps, repair robots built for a particle fountain project, are alive, and refuses to sacrifice them even when Picard and Geordi's lives are at stake.
Picard, Worf, and Crusher raid a suspected weapons lab on Celtris III while the exacting Captain Edward Jellico reshapes the Enterprise, and the mission ends in Picard's capture.
Captured by the Cardassians, Picard endures Gul Madred's torture and refuses to say he sees five lights, while Jellico mines a hidden fleet to force his release.
Still grieving the wife the Borg killed, Commander Sisko takes charge of a gutted Cardassian station over Bajor and finds a stable wormhole, becoming the Bajorans' prophesied Emissary.
Kira is torn when former resistance comrade Tahna Los seeks asylum, then buys explosives from Lursa and B'Etor to collapse the wormhole and drive the Federation away.
When Ibudan, a criminal Odo once jailed, turns up dead in a locked holosuite, suspicion falls on Odo until he proves the corpse was Ibudan's own clone.
An aphasia virus left in a replicator by the Bajoran resistance spreads across the station, scrambling speech, and Kira must track down the scientist who can cure it.
Reawakened by Barclay, Moriarty seizes the Enterprise to force his way off the holodeck with his beloved Countess, until Picard traps him in a simulation within a simulation.
Geordi falls for Lieutenant Aquiel Uhnari through her logs while she is suspected of murder at a relay station, until the killer proves to be a shape-shifting organism.
O'Brien befriends Tosk, a Gamma Quadrant native bred to be hunted, and bends the rules to free him when his hunters board the station to reclaim him.
Kidnapped and surgically disguised as a Tal Shiar officer, Troi must bluff her way through a Romulan warbird to smuggle high-ranking defectors to the Federation.
Vash returns from the Gamma Quadrant with Q in tow, and a gem she means to auction proves to be an embryo pulling the station toward the wormhole.
Given a chance by Q to avoid the youthful brawl that cost him his heart, a dying Picard takes it and becomes an unremarkable, cautious junior officer.
An informant at Deep Space 9 claims Worf's father survived Khitomer as a Romulan prisoner, and an accident gives Data his first dream, a vision of Soong.
Held in a secret camp where Khitomer survivors live peacefully beside their Romulan captors, Worf rekindles Klingon tradition in the young, and some choose to leave with him.
Returning to the evacuated Enterprise for his saddle during a lethal baryon sweep, Picard poses as a barber and battles thieves siphoning trilithium out of the warp core.
Picard falls for stellar sciences chief Nella Daren over shared music, then must order her into a firestorm on Bersallis III, after which she transfers away.
O'Brien is named Sirah of a Bajoran village and must banish the dreaded Dal'Rok, while Jake and Nog befriend Varis, a teenage leader in a land dispute.
Continuing his murdered mentor Richard Galen's work, Picard races Cardassians, Klingons, and Romulans to assemble a puzzle hidden in DNA, revealing that ancient humanoids seeded the galaxy.
Kai Opaka's runabout crashes on a moon where two factions are revived after every death to fight forever; Opaka is killed, revived, and stays to seek peace.
Rehearsing a play about madness, Riker keeps waking in an alien asylum on Tilonus IV, where captors probing his mind blur which world is real.
Arrested for murder, Gamma Quadrant fugitive Croden tempts Odo with hints about his people, and Odo ultimately lets him flee to protect his daughter.
Zek names Quark his successor and seemingly dies, making Quark Grand Nagus and a target for Rom and Krax, until Zek reveals it was all a test.
Relieved of duty for performing an unauthorized autopsy on Ferengi scientist Reyga, Crusher presses on and proves his metaphasic shield works and that his colleague Jo'Bril murdered him.
Kira must uproot Mullibok, an old farmer, from a Bajoran moon about to be tapped for power, while Jake and Nog trade yamok sauce into a land deed.
After Quark cheats the Wadi, the first Gamma Quadrant delegation to visit, they draw him into a game in which Sisko, Kira, Dax, and Bashir become living pieces.
Kahless the Unforgettable appears to Worf on Boreth, but the returned legend proves a clone made by the clerics, and Worf brokers a ceremonial throne for him.
Rumpelstiltskin, ballplayer Buck Bokai, and an adoring Jadzia double appear as the crew's fantasies take form, and even a rift menacing the Bajoran system proves imaginary.
Fugitive Rao Vantika fakes his death by hiding his consciousness inside Dr. Bashir, then uses the doctor's body in a bid to hijack a precious deuridium shipment.
Accused of a decades-old murder her previous host, Curzon, allegedly committed, Jadzia faces extradition and stays silent rather than expose his affair with the victim's wife.
Returning to Nervala IV, the crew finds Lieutenant Thomas Riker, a transporter duplicate of Will stranded there for eight years, who still loves Troi.
A telepathic relic of the extinct Saltah'na makes the senior staff replay its creators' power struggle, and only an unaffected Odo can head off Kira's mutiny.
A probe from the Gamma Quadrant leaves a playful alien program loose in the station's computer, trapping Odo in a stalled turbolift with a smitten Lwaxana Troi.
Kira's investigation of a Cardassian claiming to be Gallitep's commandant reveals Marritza, a guilt-racked clerk who wants to be executed so Cardassia must face its crimes.
Heading home by runabout, Picard, Data, Geordi, and Troi find time stopped around the Enterprise, caught in combat with a Romulan ship and seconds from annihilation.

records.ti: In the Hands of the Prophets
records.lg: Vedek Winn inflames Bajorans against Keiko's secular lessons on the wormhole, and the bombing of her school proves cover for a plot to kill the reformist Vedek Bareil.
records.ma: In the Hands of the Prophets (episode)

records.lg: Borg acting as individuals attack the Federation, and after Data feels anger in battle, he defects to their leader, his brother Lore, who promises him more emotions.
Picard, captured by Lore's Borg, must reach an emotionally manipulated Data, as Crusher fights a Borg ship with the Enterprise and Data finally deactivates Lore.
Kira and O'Brien spring resistance legend Li Nalas from a Cardassian prison camp, only to find his heroism was a fluke, as the xenophobic Circle rises on Bajor.
Relieved of her post, Kira retreats to Bareil's monastery and is abducted by the Circle, whose hidden leader is Minister Jaro, as Sisko learns Cardassia is arming it.
While Iyaaran envoys study the crew, Picard is marooned on a bleak world with Anna, whose obsessive affection turns out to be an alien's experiment in human love.
