Investigating Picard's apparent murder, Riker is taken aboard a mercenary ship raiding archaeological sites and finds Picard alive, posing as a smuggler named Galen.
Sisko's crew fights Circle troops for the station, Li Nalas dies shielding Sisko, and Kira and Dax fly an old raider to Bajor with proof of Cardassia's role.
Undercover among the mercenaries, Picard and Riker learn they are assembling the Stone of Gol, a Vulcan psionic weapon sought by an isolationist, while Data commands the Enterprise.
The case of Rugal, a Cardassian orphan raised by Bajorans, leads Garak and Bashir to a plot by Gul Dukat to disgrace the boy's politician father.
Verad, a Trill deemed unfit for joining, seizes the nearly empty station and forces Bashir to move the Dax symbiont into him, leaving Jadzia hours from death.
Remotely exploring a ship wrecked in a gas giant, Geordi, grieving his mother's vanished starship, meets an alien that takes her form to plead for help.
Data's dream program starts producing nightmares that drive him to stab Troi, and the images turn out to be warnings of invisible parasites feeding on the crew.
Bashir romances Elaysian ensign Melora Pazlar and devises a treatment letting her walk in normal gravity, which she finally declines, as a vengeful ex-partner stalks Quark.
Tutoring the telepathic Cairn aboard the Enterprise, Lwaxana collapses into a coma, and Deanna enters her mind to uncover a buried grief: an elder sister, Kestra, who drowned.
Quark negotiates a tulaberry wine deal with the Dosi for Zek, helped by his new aide Pel, a Ferengi woman in male disguise who has fallen for him.
An attack on Quark reopens Odo's first murder case from the Occupation, when Dukat drafted him as investigator, and leads him to learn that Kira was the killer.
Imprisoned by paranoid Prytt security forces, Picard and Crusher escape with brain implants that link their thoughts, exposing feelings the two have long left unspoken.
Hekaran scientists Rabal and Serova claim warp drive is tearing subspace apart, and when Serova sacrifices herself to prove it, the Federation imposes a warp speed limit.
On the anniversary of his wife's death, Sisko falls for the elusive Fenna, who proves to be a telepathic projection of Nidell, the unhappy wife of a terraformer.
Back from a bat'leth competition, Worf slips between parallel realities, in one married to Troi, until thousands of Enterprises converge and he must find his own.
Skrreean refugees led by Haneek arrive via the wormhole believing Bajor is Kentanna, their prophesied homeland, but the struggling Bajorans turn them away, with tragic results.
El-Aurian con man Martus Mazur opens a rival bar with a gambling device that warps probability across the station, as O'Brien becomes fixated on beating Bashir at racquetball.
Odo's old mentor Dr. Mora Pol finds a lead on Odo's people, but a creature stalking the station proves to be Odo himself, changed by volcanic gas.
Helping to save Atrea IV, Data meets Soong's former wife Juliana Tainer and learns she is an android replica of the original, a secret he keeps from her.
Worf's foster brother Nikolai, defying the Prime Directive, hides a village from dying Boraal II in a holodeck, and Worf helps guide them to a new home.
Admiral Erik Pressman, Riker's first captain, joins the hunt for the Pegasus, which hides an illegal cloaking device, forcing Riker to choose between loyalty and exposing the cover-up.
After helping the T'Lani and Kellerun destroy their bioweapons, O'Brien and Bashir are hunted by both governments, who want no one alive who knows how the weapons worked.
At her grandmother's funeral on the Scottish-styled colony Caldos, Beverly Crusher is seduced by Ronin, a ghostly entity bound to her family's candle, who wants her next.
Facing a hard choice, Riker relives on the Enterprise-D holodeck the final mission of Archer's Enterprise, on the eve of the Federation's founding, in which Trip dies.
Junior officers vying for promotion puzzle over their superiors' secretive actions, until Ensign Sito Jaxa volunteers for a covert mission into Cardassian space and never returns.
Stranded on a colony where no technology works, Sisko endures a punishment box while O'Brien exposes Alixus, the leader who secretly created the field trapping everyone.
Back from the Parada system, O'Brien grows convinced his crewmates are conspiring against him, never suspecting he is a Paradan replicant built to sabotage peace talks.
Investigating disappearances in a Gamma Quadrant village, Odo and Dax learn its residents are holograms kept by a lonely exile from the Dominion, and Odo befriends a girl.
Amnesiac and carrying radioactive debris, Data unknowingly sickens a pre-industrial village, while Troi seeks a promotion that requires her to send a simulated Geordi to his death.
An archive hidden in a comet transforms the Enterprise into a D'Arsay temple and fills Data with alien personas, until Picard plays the moon god Korgano.
Looking into a crewman's suicide, Troi uncovers telepathic echoes of a murder committed during the Enterprise's construction at Utopia Planitia, and begins reliving it herself.
While mentoring Trill initiate Arjin, Dax finds a tiny, swelling protouniverse that may hold life, and the crew must return it before it consumes the Bajoran system.
Crusher's synthetic T-cell treatment for Barclay goes airborne and devolves the crew into primitive creatures, leaving Data and a slowly changing Picard to find a cure.
Quark's old flame Natima Lang arrives as a fugitive Cardassian dissident, and he schemes to win her back and smuggle her out, with surprising help from Garak.
Kang, Kor, and Koloth invoke Curzon's blood oath against the Albino, killer of their sons, and Jadzia joins a raid in which the Albino, Kang, and Koloth die.
Ordered to evict Native American colonists from Dorvan V, ceded to Cardassia by treaty, Picard is defied by Wesley, who leaves Starfleet to study with the Traveler.
The bombing of a Cardassian freighter leads Sisko to the Maquis, Federation settlers fighting back in the Demilitarized Zone, whose ranks include his old friend Cal Hudson.
The mysterious K'mtar pushes young Alexander toward a warrior's path to protect Worf from the Duras sisters, and turns out to be Alexander himself, back from the future.
Sisko recovers the kidnapped Dukat, exposes Cardassian arms smuggling in the zone, and faces down his friend Cal Hudson to keep a Maquis strike from igniting war.
Still seeking revenge, DaiMon Bok threatens to kill Jason Vigo, a young man he says is Picard's son, though the tie proves to be Bok's genetic forgery.
Bashir treats Garak for a failing Obsidian Order implant he has abused like a drug, hears three conflicting tales of his exile, and turns to Enabran Tain.
A wormhole mishap strands Kira and Bashir in the mirror universe, where humans are slaves, Kira's ruthless double runs the station, and their escape sparks a Terran revolt.
A holodeck train ride gone strange reveals the Enterprise is developing a mind of its own and assembling an offspring the crew must help bring to life.
Kira probes claims that Bareil betrayed a resistance cell and finds Kai Opaka did it; to shield Opaka's legacy, Bareil withdraws from the Kai race and Winn wins.
Sent undercover to lure a Maquis cell into a Starfleet trap, Ro Laren comes to share their cause and finally betrays Picard to join the rebels.
Seized on vacation, O'Brien faces a rigged Cardassian show trial for aiding the Maquis, until Odo and Sisko expose the frame-up behind it.
Sisko's Gamma Quadrant outing with Jake, Nog, and Quark ends with capture by the Jem'Hadar, enforcers of the Dominion, whose suicide run destroys the rescuing USS Odyssey.
Warned by Q, Picard shifts among his first mission, the present, and a future twenty-five years on to stop an anomaly of his own making from unmaking humanity.
With the warship Defiant, Sisko ventures into the Gamma Quadrant to find the Dominion's rulers, and Odo, drawn to the Omarion Nebula, finally finds his people.
Odo learns his people are the Dominion's Founders, as Sisko watches the Federation accept a ruinous peace deal, a scenario that turns out to be the Founders' test.
Quark's bogus boast of killing a Klingon gets him abducted and wed by the widow Grilka, and on Qo'noS his ledgers save her house from the scheming D'Ghor.
Haunting visions send Jadzia to Trill, where Sisko and Bashir uncover a host the Symbiosis Commission erased from Dax's record: Joran, a musician and murderer.
Hauled into the Delta Quadrant with the Maquis ship it was chasing, Voyager forfeits a quick trip home when Janeway destroys the Caretaker's array to protect the Ocampa.
The Obsidian Order abducts Kira and insists she is Iliana Ghemor, a surgically altered sleeper agent, in a ploy to unmask her supposed father as a dissident.
Salvage bought by Quark holds an infant that grows within days into a Jem'Hadar soldier, and Odo tries to raise him beyond his programming before letting him go.
A forgotten Cardassian anti-riot program, triggered by accident, treats the station as seized by Bajoran rebels and locks it down ever tighter, trapping even Dukat.
Jadzia falls for Deral of Meridian, a planet that drops out of normal space for sixty-year spans, as Quark schemes to sell a holosuite likeness of Kira.
Voyager's own reflected distress call lures it into a quantum singularity's event horizon, and B'Elanna Torres wins the chief engineer's post by helping get the ship out.
Posing as his transporter twin Will, Thomas Riker hijacks the Defiant for the Maquis, and Sisko joins Dukat to hunt him as he uncovers an Obsidian Order fleet.
During the Bajoran Gratitude Festival, Lwaxana Troi's Zanthi fever sets off mismatched passions across the station, from Jake's crush on Kira to Bareil's sudden pursuit of Dax.
A transporter mishap strands Sisko, Bashir, and Dax in 2024 San Francisco, where Gabriel Bell, a pivotal figure of history, dies saving Sisko, who must take his place.
As Gabriel Bell, Sisko sees the Bell Riots through to their historic end, risking his life to shield hostages, while Kira and O'Brien search through time for them.
Bashir sustains a dying Vedek Bareil with artificial brain implants so he can steer Kai Winn's peace talks with Cardassia, even as the man himself fades away.
Surveying a world wiped out by a polaric explosion, Janeway and Paris slip back a day and find their own rescue attempt may cause the disaster.
A crystal engulfing Kira on a moon prompts Odo to confess his love, and her reply exposes her as the Female Changeling; Nog seeks Sisko's backing for Starfleet.
Vidiian organ harvesters, ravaged by a disease called the phage, steal Neelix's lungs, and the Doctor keeps him alive with holographic ones until Kes donates a lung.
Vedek Yarka warns a doomsday prophecy is unfolding as Cardassian scientists help Sisko build a communications relay through the wormhole, and the omens come true in unexpected ways.
Voyager's search for energy inside a nebula wounds what turns out to be a living organism, and Janeway takes the ship back in to heal it.
A tiny wormhole connects Voyager to a Romulan ship in the Alpha Quadrant, but the scientist aboard, Telek R'Mor, is living twenty years in the past.
Zek returns preaching charity from a rewritten Rules of Acquisition, so Quark hauls him to the Prophets to undo it, while Bashir frets over a Carrington Award nomination.
Convicted on Banea of murdering a scientist, Tom Paris is sentenced to relive the killing through the victim's eyes, until Tuvok proves the memories were planted for espionage.
Radiation sends O'Brien skipping hours ahead in time, where he sees his death and the station's destruction, and he must expose a Romulan plot to collapse the wormhole.
Pulled through a subspace rift to the Vhnori homeworld, Harry Kim challenges their belief in an afterlife by describing the asteroid where their dead end up.
El-Aurian Soran will destroy stars to reenter the Nexus, and Picard, having lost the Enterprise-D, recruits Kirk, trapped there since 2293, who dies stopping him.
The pleasure-loving Sikarians own a spatial trajector that could fling Voyager 40,000 light-years toward home, but refuse to share it, tempting Tuvok and Torres into a secret trade.
A Lethean's telepathic assault leaves Bashir comatose in a dreamscape of the station, where he ages by decades and his crewmates embody pieces of his own mind.
When Voyager technology turns up aboard a Kazon ship, the hunt for a traitor exposes Seska, a Cardassian agent posing as a Bajoran, who defects to the Kazon.
When crew members vanish within Harry Kim's Beowulf holonovel, the Doctor makes his first away mission and discovers photonic aliens are taking them.
Abducted into the mirror universe to pose as his dead counterpart, Sisko must turn Jennifer's double, a scientist aiding the Alliance, to the Terran rebels' cause.
The bombing of Garak's shop, which Garak staged himself, leads Odo to Enabran Tain and a secret Romulan-Cardassian fleet poised to strike the Founders' homeworld.
With Chakotay left brain-dead, his consciousness leaps between crewmates to steer Voyager away from a nebula where aliens feed on neural energy.
Back in Tain's service, Garak interrogates Odo as the Romulan-Cardassian fleet attacks the Founders' world and meets a Dominion ambush, and Sisko defies orders to save them.
A Vidiian scientist hunting a phage cure splits B'Elanna Torres into a human woman and a Klingon one, who must rely on each other to escape.
Recreating an ancient Bajoran solar-sail ship, Sisko and Jake ride tachyon eddies all the way to Cardassia, proving that early Bajorans could have made the voyage.
Jetrel, whose weapon killed hundreds of thousands of Talaxians on Rinax, claims Neelix may be ill as cover for an attempt to restore the dead.
Liquidator Brunt shutters Quark's bar until Quark returns to Ferenginar to deal with his mother, Ishka, who has illegally earned profit; Jake sets Sisko up with Kasidy Yates.
Tuvok puts four undisciplined Maquis crewmen through Starfleet training, while the ship's bio-neural circuitry falls sick with an infection traced to Neelix's cheese.
Ordered by Winn to seize farm equipment from Shakaar, her old resistance leader, Kira joins him instead, and the standoff ends with Shakaar unseating Winn as First Minister.
Damaged by a radiation surge, the Doctor is told by a holographic Reginald Barclay that he is really his own creator, Lewis Zimmerman, trapped in a Voyager simulation.
In the Trill zhian'tara rite, Jadzia meets her past hosts through her friends' bodies, confronting the murderous Joran and a Curzon who, housed in Odo, refuses to leave.
Space-dwelling creatures draw Voyager into their mating rituals, while their energy triggers Kes's elogium, the Ocampa's one chance to conceive, forcing her and Neelix to decide on parenthood.
A distortion ring engulfs Voyager and rearranges its corridors into a shrinking maze, and the crew's only way out is to stop fighting it and wait.
Sisko's first mission as captain is a trap: the ambassador aboard the Defiant is a Changeling bent on sparking a war, and Odo kills one of his own.
A Ford pickup from 1936, adrift in space, leads Voyager to Amelia Earhart and other humans abducted in 1937, whose descendants now thrive on a distant planet.
Chakotay is attacked during a solo ritual by Kar, a Kazon youth who must kill an enemy to earn his name, and tries to show him another way.
Harry Kim wakes in San Francisco beside his fiancée Libby, in a timeline where he never joined Voyager, and must re-create the shuttle accident that put him there.
Recruited by Sisko to probe a Klingon fleet's arrival, Worf uncovers an invasion of Cardassia that shatters the Khitomer Accords and brings a Klingon assault on the station.
An elderly Jake recounts how an accident left his father unstuck in time, surfacing briefly across the decades, and how Jake gave his life to set things right.
Feuding over Kes, Paris and Neelix are stranded together on a hostile planet, where caring for a newly hatched reptilian creature forces them to work out their differences.
Captured by Jem'Hadar deserters, Bashir tries to free them from their ketracel-white addiction while O'Brien works to escape, and on the station Worf clashes with Odo over Quark.
An exhausted Janeway and her crew are overwhelmed by hallucinations drawn from their memories and fantasies, and only Kes can resist the telepathic alien behind them.
A symbol matching Chakotay's tribal markings leads him to the Sky Spirits, aliens who shaped his ancestors, stirring memories of a youthful jungle trek with his father.
Searching with Dukat for the lost prison ship Ravinok, Kira learns he is after his half-Bajoran daughter Ziyal, whom he plans to kill before relenting.
Searching for the Caretaker's mate, Suspiria, Voyager finds an Ocampa colony whose leader, Tanis, trains Kes to amplify her mental powers toward sinister ends.
After a Changeling bombing on Earth, Sisko returns to San Francisco to lead Starfleet security under Admiral Leyton, and a planetwide blackout pushes the president toward emergency rule.
A transporter emergency stores the senior staff inside Bashir's 1960s spy holosuite fantasy, and he and Garak must play the story out without killing their friends.
Lenara Kahn, whose symbiont was wed to a past Dax host, rekindles a romance with Jadzia that ends when she refuses to break the Trill taboo against reassociation.
After Seska helps the Kazon steal a transporter module, Chakotay pursues them alone and is captured and tortured, and Seska secretly takes his DNA to conceive a child.
Kor, Worf, and Dax recover the Sword of Kahless from a Gamma Quadrant world, but it sets the Klingons against each other, so Worf beams it into space.
Flying Nog to Starfleet Academy, Quark and Rom, with Odo stowed away, are thrown back to 1947 Roswell, where the U.S. military takes the Ferengi for alien invaders.
To free Tuvok and Torres from the Mokra, Janeway accepts help from Caylem, a delusional old rebel who believes she is his long-lost daughter.
Hiding in a gas giant after defending a Karemma ship, the crippled Defiant stalks the Jem'Hadar while Kira keeps a wounded Sisko awake and Worf learns to lead.
A robot Torres revives, Automated Unit 3947, abducts her to build more of its kind, and she learns its race killed its makers and wages endless war.
Freed from a comet prison, a Q called Quinn requests asylum in order to die, and Janeway must rule on his plea as Q argues against it.
Battered by Kazon attacks, Janeway seeks allies, first among the Kazon and then with their former masters, the Trabe, whose leader turns peace talks into an ambush.
Sisko learns the blackout was sabotage by Red Squad cadets serving Admiral Leyton, and races to stop the admiral's coup to put Earth under martial law.
In a modified shuttle, Tom Paris breaks the warp 10 barrier, but the feat starts mutating him into a new species, and he abducts Janeway, who changes too.
To understand why crewman Lon Suder killed a shipmate for no reason, Tuvok mind-melds with him and absorbs his violent impulses, losing his own emotional control.
Guarding First Minister Shakaar from assassins, Odo watches Kira fall for the man, and his hidden heartbreak leaves him smashing his quarters and nearly failing at his job.
Torres's old Maquis project, a reprogrammed Cardassian missile called Dreadnought, turns up in the Delta Quadrant targeting a populated world, and she must outthink her own programming.
Using his new shipboard news program, Neelix investigates Tom Paris's sudden departure and uncovers both Paris's undercover mission and the real traitor, Michael Jonas.
Disgraced for acknowledging his half-Bajoran daughter, Dukat ferries Kira to a conference the Klingons destroy, and the two capture a Bird-of-Prey that Dukat turns to his own war.
The Doctor falls for Danara Pel, a Vidiian physician whose mind he places in a healthy holographic body while treating her, as Tom Paris grows openly insubordinate.
A spatial rift duplicates Voyager, and when Vidiians overrun one copy, its Janeway destroys it to save the other, which takes in its Harry Kim and a newborn.
Disgraced by Worf's stand against Gowron, Kurn begs his brother to kill him, and Worf ultimately has Kurn's memories erased so he can start a new life.
Stranded on a moon, Tuvok protects frightened children who keep disappearing, then learns they are Drayan elders nearing death in a species that ages backward.
Rom unionizes Quark's staff and leads them on strike over wages and conditions, defying Quark and the FCA's Brunt, then quits to become a station engineer.
Trying to wake survivors from stasis pods, Harry Kim and Torres are trapped in a virtual world ruled by a sadistic clown, the embodiment of the sleepers' fear.
Legendary poet Akorem Laan emerges from the wormhole claiming to be the Emissary, and after he revives Bajor's caste system, Sisko reclaims the role he never wanted.
A transporter accident merges Tuvok and Neelix into Tuvix, and when a way to separate them is found, Janeway must end a life that begs to continue.
Klingon advocate Ch'Pok seeks Worf's extradition after the Defiant, under his command, destroys a civilian transport, until Odo proves its passengers were already dead.
Infected with a virus only their new planet holds at bay, Janeway and Chakotay settle into a life together, until Tuvok defies orders to get a Vidiian cure.
The Argrathi punish O'Brien with false memories of two decades behind bars, and back home, guilt over killing his cellmate Ee'Char nearly drives him to suicide.
The mirror Jennifer lures Jake across universes to draw Sisko into helping the Terran rebels finish their own Defiant, which he commands against the Regent Worf's fleet.
The alluring Onaya inspires Jake's first novel while feeding on his life force, and a pregnant Lwaxana Troi weds Odo to keep her son from his Tavnian father.
Seska's claim that she has borne Chakotay's son draws Voyager into a Kazon-Nistrim ambush, and Culluh seizes the ship and maroons its crew on a primitive world.
Sisko faces evidence that Kasidy Yates smuggles for the Maquis, but the deeper betrayal is Lieutenant Eddington's, as he steals a cargo of industrial replicators and defects.
After renegade Jem'Hadar raid the station, Sisko forms an uneasy alliance with the Vorta Weyoun and his loyal soldiers to destroy an Iconian gateway the rebels have seized.
Bashir's attempt to cure a Dominion-engineered blight on a Gamma Quadrant world fails, but it yields a vaccine that lets the next generation be born healthy.
Wrongly told he is dying, Quark sells his remains, then learns the buyer is Brunt, who expects delivery, while Kira carries the O'Briens' baby after an accident.
A Founder-induced illness brings Odo to the Great Link, where he is punished for killing a changeling by being made human, and comes away believing Gowron is one.
Marooned on Hanon IV, the crew fights natives and predators to survive, while Lon Suder and the Doctor sabotage the Kazon aboard Voyager and Paris brings help.
Disguised as Klingons, Sisko's team infiltrates a Klingon stronghold to unmask Gowron as a Changeling, only to discover the impostor is actually General Martok.
Holding a crashed Jem'Hadar ship against the Vorta Kilana's siege, Sisko loses crewman Muniz, then learns her real prize was a Founder dying inside the wreck.
When Kes collapses after trespassing in a Nechani shrine, Janeway undergoes the monks' baffling spiritual trials to save her, setting aside her trust in science.
Arridor and Kol, Ferengi stranded by the Barzan wormhole, rule a primitive world as revered sages, and Voyager must unseat them beside an unstable wormhole leading home.
A mind-meld meant to cure Tuvok's hallucinations takes Janeway into his years on Captain Sulu's Excelsior, where a memory virus has lurked for decades.
Wrongly jailed for an Akritirian bombing, Tom Paris and Harry Kim land in a brutal prison where a neural clamp slowly drives inmates mad, testing their friendship.
While Voyager ferries Enaran passengers, Torres dreams through the eyes of a young Enaran who saw her people wipe out a dissident group, a genocide they have erased.
Voyager cuts through territory guarded by an alien swarm while the Doctor's program begins to degrade, forcing Kes and a holographic copy of his creator to save him.

records.ti: Looking for par'Mach in All the Wrong Places
records.lg: Worf coaches Quark in Klingon courtship to win back his ex-wife Grilka, even fighting a duel for him by remote control, and ends up falling for Jadzia himself.
records.ma: Looking for par'Mach in All the Wrong Places (episode)

records.lg: Attacked by a 29th-century timeship, Voyager is thrown back to 1996 Los Angeles, where tech mogul Henry Starling has built his fortune on salvaged future technology.
Before Henry Starling can fly his stolen timeship into the future and devastate it, Janeway must stop him, aided by astronomer Rain Robinson and a newly mobile Doctor.
The dying Ilari warlord Tieran transfers his mind into Kes, using her body to seize power on his homeworld, while Kes fights to reclaim herself.
Hoping a child will end the Continuum's civil war, Q proposes having one with Janeway, who is drawn into the conflict and steers him toward a female Q.
As her old Shakaar comrades are murdered one by one, a pregnant Kira tracks the killer, a scarred Cardassian who blames her for the innocents her bombs harmed.
Returning from a trade mission, Janeway finds Voyager overrun by giant airborne viruses, and she and the Doctor must fight through the crippled ship to spread an antigen.
Afraid of becoming useless as Voyager enters space he doesn't know, Neelix joins an old friend's shady deal, which turns deadly and buries him in lies.
Odo raises a fragile infant Changeling and makes peace with Dr. Mora, and the dying baby's merger with Odo restores his shape-shifting, as Kira delivers the O'Briens' son.
Harry Kim falls for holodeck character Marayna, who prefers Tuvok and proves to be the avatar of a lonely alien seizing control of Voyager from a nearby nebula.
Visions triggered by an accident lead Sisko to the lost city of B'hala and warn him Bajor must not yet join the Federation, but they are killing him.
When Maquis turncoat Michael Eddington poisons a Cardassian colony, an obsessed Sisko retaliates by poisoning a Maquis world to force his surrender.

records.ti: Nor the Battle to the Strong
records.lg: Traveling with Bashir, Jake lands at a field hospital under Klingon siege on Ajilon Prime, panics and flees under fire, and writes an honest account of his fear.
records.ma: Nor the Battle to the Strong (episode)

records.lg: Caught in repeated deaths after a shuttle crash, Janeway is urged toward the afterlife by her father, until she recognizes him as an alien preying on her mind.
Stranded on a barren world by a bomb, Quark and Odo must haul each other up a mountain to call for help, while Nog moves in with Jake.
Following a coded signal, Garak and Worf land in a Dominion prison camp with Tain, the real Martok, and the real Bashir, whose station double is a Changeling.
Vorik's pon farr spreads to B'Elanna Torres, who turns her fevered attentions on Tom Paris during an away mission that ends with the discovery of a dead Borg.
Dukat leads Cardassia into the Dominion as its fleet emerges, a Changeling posing as Bashir tries to destroy Bajor's sun, and Worf and Garak lead a camp breakout.
Odo, Sisko, Dax, and Garak wake on Occupation-era Terok Nor as Bajorans condemned to death, an illusion that forces Odo to confront an execution he once allowed.
Lewis Zimmerman models a new medical hologram on Bashir, exposing Julian's secret, illegal genetic enhancement as a child, and his father accepts prison to save his son's career.
Nursed by former Borg drones on a war-torn world, Chakotay learns his rescuers want to link minds, his included, into a new collective of their own.

records.ti: Let He Who Is Without Sin...
records.lg: A vacation on Risa goes sour for Worf and Dax when Worf, bristling at the planet's indulgence, joins the Essentialists, a movement plotting to sabotage its weather control.
records.ma: Let He Who Is Without Sin... (episode)

records.lg: Odo falls for Arissa, a woman marked for death by the Orion Syndicate, and finds his first love, only to lose her to the family she left behind.
Deep in debt, Quark joins his cousin Gaila's arms-dealing business, but when a deal would arm a genocidal regent, his conscience drives him to sabotage it.
Klingon spy Arne Darvin drags the Defiant to 2268 to kill Kirk on Space Station K-7, and the crew blends into history, tribbles and all, to stop him.
Adding traits of famous historical figures to his program, the Doctor unleashes a violent alter ego, while Kes considers leaving Voyager for Zahir, a charming Mikhal traveler.
Kira nurses her dying surrogate father, the Cardassian dissident Tekeny Ghemor, as Dukat and Weyoun press for his extradition and she confronts memories of her own father's death.
Helping the Nezu fend off asteroid strikes, Tuvok and Neelix are stranded with survivors who must ride an orbital tether to escape, while a killer hides among them.
Possessing Keiko, a Pah-wraith forces O'Brien to rig the station to fire on the wormhole and kill the Prophets, until he and Rom turn the plan against it.
Markings and new abilities convince Harry Kim he is a Taresian, but the planet of welcoming women who claim him turns out to harvest the men it lures.
Home on Ferenginar, Quark finds his mother Ishka romancing Zek and, bribed by Brunt, splits them up, then learns she has been secretly guiding the failing Nagus.
As first officer of the demoralized Rotarran, Worf goads a shaken Martok into a duel to restore his nerve, and earns a place in the House of Martok.
An elderly Kes slides backward through her future life, witnessing a war with the Krenim and a family with Tom Paris, toward her own birth.
The Defiant crew meets its 8,000 descendants, born of a crash into the past still ahead of them, and an elder Odo seals their fate for Kira's sake.
When Torres makes the Doctor's idealized holographic family more realistic, he faces a rebellious son and a dying daughter, while Paris gets trapped probing a subspace vortex.
Sisko drags the jailed Eddington along to find Maquis missiles aimed at Cardassia, but the launch is a bluff to save Maquis survivors, and Eddington dies protecting them.
Voth scientist Forra Gegen finds proof that his saurian people came from Earth, but Voth leaders defending doctrine force him to recant to spare Chakotay.
Joining a Borg battle against orders, Picard pursues a Borg sphere back to 2063, where he must protect Zefram Cochrane's first warp flight and confront the Borg Queen.
Salvaging parts from Empok Nor, DS9's abandoned twin, O'Brien's team is picked off by drug-crazed Cardassian soldiers, and when the drug infects Garak, O'Brien must outwit him.
One by one, Voyager's crew is swapped for Nyrians, quiet aliens who take over the ship while moving its people into a sprawling habitat of captive environments.
Hoping to cheer Sisko, Jake and Nog trade favors across the station to land a 1951 Willie Mays card, while Weyoun offers Bajor a nonaggression pact.
Crew members get hooked on a holonovel about a Maquis mutiny, written by Tuvok as a training exercise, until a booby trap left by Seska turns it deadly.
Sisko seals the wormhole with self-replicating mines, and when Dukat's fleet retakes the station, Starfleet withdraws, leaving Kira, Odo, and Quark behind as Sisko vows to return.
In Borg space, Voyager finds the Collective being overrun by Species 8472, and Janeway strikes a deal with the Borg: a weapon against the invaders for safe passage.
With Janeway injured, Chakotay must manage the uneasy alliance with the Borg, whose drone liaison, Seven of Nine, is cut off from the Collective and left aboard Voyager.
As a resentful Seven of Nine is weaned from the Borg, Kes's mental powers surge beyond control, and she leaves, flinging Voyager years closer to home.
On the Klingon Day of Honor, Torres and Tom Paris end up adrift in space with failing air and confess their feelings, while Borg-ravaged Caatati refugees demand help.
With the war going badly, Sisko takes a captured Jem'Hadar ship behind enemy lines to destroy the Dominion's ketracel-white depot, while Kira and Odo live uneasily under occupation.
Stranded amid a war between the Vori and the Kradin, Chakotay fights beside the Vori and learns to hate their enemy, not realizing he is being carefully indoctrinated.
Stranded on an ocean world, Sisko's crew faces Jem'Hadar short of ketracel-white whose Vorta sells them out, and a Bajoran's suicide spurs Kira to resist the Dominion.
Worf's son Alexander enlists on the Rotarran, forcing father and son to confront their past, while Dukat uses Ziyal's return to Terok Nor to draw closer to Kira.
The Female Changeling draws Odo into linking with her as Kira's resistance cell needs him to thwart the Dominion's plan to clear the minefield, and Rom is captured.
Sisko persuades Starfleet to mount a fleet to retake the station before the minefield falls, while a captured Rom faces execution and Kira's cell fights to free him.
The Doctor and Torres answer a distress call from Dejaren, a hologram who loathes organic life and has murdered his ship's crew, as Harry Kim falls for Seven.
Krenim scientist Annorax uses a weapon ship that erases species from history to restore his empire, and the changes leave Voyager battered through a grueling year of attacks.
Sisko's Defiant punches through the Dominion lines alone, the Prophets make an entire enemy armada vanish in the wormhole at a price, and Ziyal's death shatters Dukat.
Plagued by flashbacks she takes for a Borg summons, Seven steals a shuttle and finds the wrecked Raven, the ship where she was assimilated as a child.
Invisible Srivani scientists are secretly experimenting on the crew, and once Seven and the Doctor expose them, a stressed-out Janeway steers between two stars to drive them off.
Worf and Jadzia move up their wedding, but Martok's wife Sirella objects to the bride, and the ordeal of Klingon rites nearly ends the marriage before it begins.
The mirror universe's Bareil arrives seeking refuge and wins Kira's heart, but he is a thief working with the Intendant to steal a Bajoran Orb.
Bashir enlists a band of genetically enhanced misfits to analyze enemy data, but their projections lead them to urge surrender and try to leak secrets to the Dominion.
Arrested by the telepathic Mari after her flash of anger fuels a murder, Torres faces a mind purge while Tuvok uncovers a black market in violent thoughts.
To ransom his captured mother, Quark assembles a Ferengi crew, Brunt included, to swap the Vorta Keevan for her on Empok Nor, a plan that soon goes awry.
When raiders steal Voyager's main computer and the Doctor's mobile emitter, Janeway tracks them to a planet where her holographic Leonardo da Vinci now serves the thief.
After the Honshu is destroyed, an injured Sisko is stranded with a deranged Dukat, whose hallucinated arguments peel away his self-justifications until he embraces his hatred of Bajorans.
Morn's apparent death leaves Quark his estate, drawing Morn's former partners, who want a share of latinum from an old heist, until Morn turns out to be alive.
Brought back by Seven's nanoprobes eighteen hours after dying, Neelix recalls no Great Forest afterlife, and the loss of his faith drives him toward suicide.
The Prophets cast Sisko as Benny Russell, a Black writer in 1950s New York whose tale of a Black space station captain his editors refuse to print.
Beamed across an alien relay network to the Prometheus, the Doctor must retake the ship from Romulans with its own EMH, then tells Starfleet that Voyager survives.
The crew's nightmares share the same menacing alien, and Chakotay must use lucid dreaming to confront a species that lives in dreams and is trapping them asleep.
Shrunk with their runabout while studying a spatial anomaly, Dax, O'Brien, and Bashir must fly inside the Defiant's circuitry to help Sisko retake it from Jem'Hadar boarders.
Letters from home arrive through the Hirogen relay network, with news that the Maquis are gone and Janeway's fiancé has married, as Hirogen hunters capture Tuvok and Seven.
Undercover in the Orion Syndicate for Starfleet Intelligence, O'Brien grows close to Bilby, a small-time crook, and must betray him to stop a Dominion-backed assassination.
With Voyager nearly destroyed and Chakotay and Paris held by Annorax, Janeway rams her ship into his timeship, erasing the whole year and returning him to his wife.
Worf abandons a mission on Soukara to save a gravely wounded Jadzia, a choice that may cost him his career, as O'Brien and Bashir tackle Quark at tongo.

records.ti: Wrongs Darker Than Death or Night
records.lg: Stung by Dukat's claim about her mother, Kira steps through the Orb of Time into the Occupation and learns Meru became his mistress to keep her family alive.
records.ma: Wrongs Darker Than Death or Night (episode)

records.lg: Voyager rescues a Hirogen hunter tracking a stranded member of Species 8472, and when Janeway tries to send the creature home, Seven defies her and hands it over.
Under the Doctor's guidance, Seven recovers memories of being assaulted by the weapons trader Kovin, but the accusation proves mistaken only after it drives him to his death.
Accused of spying for the Dominion by the investigator Sloan, Bashir learns the ordeal was a test by Section 31, a covert Starfleet body eager to recruit him.
The Hirogen seize Voyager and implant the crew with false identities, hunting them through holodeck battles from Klingon warfare to occupied France in World War II.
As the World War II simulation spills beyond the holodeck, Janeway and Seven regain their identities and fight to retake Voyager, offering the Hirogen the holographic technology itself.
Sisko has Garak forge evidence to pull Romulus into the war; when the forgery is caught, Garak murders Senator Vreenak, and Sisko concludes he can live with it.
Vic Fontaine, a self-aware holographic lounge singer, coaches Odo in romance, and after a mix-up with a holographic stand-in, Odo finally tells Kira he loves her.
Restless Tom Paris befriends Steth, a test pilot flying a coaxial warp drive, who turns out to be a body thief and swaps appearances with him.
Janeway follows a secret order to destroy subspace-shattering Omega molecules, while Seven, raised by the Borg to revere Omega as perfection, longs to study it first.
An ancient tablet from B'hala heralds the Reckoning, in which a Prophet inhabits Kira and a Pah-wraith seizes Jake, until Kai Winn halts the battle.
Kellin, a Ramuran whose people leave no trace in others' memories, seeks asylum and rekindles a forgotten romance with Chakotay, until her people erase her memory instead.
Rescued by the Valiant, a warship crewed by Red Squad cadets, Jake and Nog watch its zealous captain lead it into a doomed attack on a Dominion battleship.
Zek is ousted as Nagus for backing women's rights, and to keep Brunt from taking over, Quark briefly becomes a woman, Lumba, to win over the influential Nilva.
Desperate for deuterium, Voyager lands on a lethal Demon-class planet, where a sentient silver fluid copies Paris and Kim, and Janeway lets it duplicate the whole crew.
Retrieved from a time portal on Golana as a feral eighteen-year-old, Molly O'Brien cannot adjust, and her parents make a wrenching choice to restore her childhood.
With the crew in stasis to cross a deadly nebula, Seven and the Doctor run Voyager by themselves, and when his program fails, solitude begins to break her.
The Defiant crew bonds by radio with Captain Lisa Cusak, stranded on a hostile planet, only to arrive and find a time distortion meant she died years before.
Brushing aside the Prophets' warning, Sisko commands the Federation offensive at Chin'toka, while Dukat, possessed by a Pah-wraith, kills Jadzia and closes the wormhole.
The alien linguist Arturis helps decode Starfleet's message and leads Voyager to the Dauntless, a slipstream ship he built as a trap to deliver them to the Borg.
Crossing a starless expanse, a guilt-stricken Janeway withdraws from her crew, until they discover Malon freighters dumping toxic waste that is killing the region's hidden inhabitants.
Grieving in New Orleans, Sisko follows a vision to the secret of his real mother, Sarah, as Worf seeks a glorious battle to send Jadzia's spirit to Sto-Vo-Kor.

A transporter accident fuses Seven's nanoprobes with the Doctor's 29th-century emitter, creating One, a gentle advanced Borg who ultimately sacrifices himself to keep the Collective from claiming him.
While the crew builds the Delta Flyer to reach a probe in a gas giant, Torres numbs her grief for the Maquis with deadly holodeck risks.
Voyager discovers Species 8472 training infiltrators in a replica of Starfleet Academy, and Chakotay goes undercover there before Janeway negotiates a wary peace.
While her mother is trapped in the crashed Delta Flyer, Neelix keeps young Naomi Wildman distracted with holodeck fairy tales, reliving his own family's loss.
Fifteen years after a slipstream flight crashed Voyager on an ice planet, Chakotay and Harry Kim defy Starfleet to send a correction back in time and save everyone.
Sisko finds the Orb of the Emissary and reopens the wormhole, Worf's team hits a Dominion shipyard, Kira blockades the Romulans, and Ezri Dax arrives.
Demoted and jailed for thirty days, Tom Paris writes his father a letter explaining how he defied Janeway to save an ocean world by sabotaging its oxygen refinery.
Newly joined and unsure of herself, Ezri Dax becomes the station's counselor and helps Garak through a breakdown rooted in guilt over betraying Cardassia, while Worf resents her.

records.ti: Take Me Out to the Holosuite
records.lg: Goaded by his old Vulcan rival Solok, Sisko drills his inept crew into a baseball team, and they lose to the Logicians but celebrate a single hard-won run.
records.ma: Take Me Out to the Holosuite (episode)

records.lg: Bashir brings Sarina, the catatonic member of the genetically enhanced group, into full awareness, then falls in love with her before realizing she needs time to find herself.
Hiding telepathic refugees from Devore inspectors, Janeway grows close to the charming Inspector Kashyk, who claims he wants to defect, in a game of deception she finally wins.

records.ti: Treachery, Faith and the Great River
records.lg: A flawed Weyoun clone defects to Odo, revealing the Founders are dying of a disease, as Nog trusts the Great Material Continuum to find O'Brien a spare part.
records.ma: Treachery, Faith and the Great River (episode)

records.lg: To remove an alien creature clinging to Torres, the Doctor consults a hologram of Crell Moset, a Cardassian exobiologist whose knowledge came from experiments on Bajorans.
Aging warrior Kor seeks one last battle, but Martok, who bears an old grudge, blocks him, until Kor takes on a suicide mission to cover the fleet's retreat.
Researching her ancestor Shannon O'Donnel, whom family legend credits with building the Millennium Gate, Janeway learns the real story involved a stubborn Indiana bookstore owner in 2000.
Finding gaps in his memory, the Doctor uncovers a deleted crisis in which he saved Harry Kim instead of Ensign Jetal, a choice whose guilt broke his program.
Delivering supplies to AR-558, a captured Dominion relay held by exhausted Starfleet troops, Sisko's crew stays to defend it against a Jem'Hadar assault, and Nog loses his leg.
Abducted to Empok Nor, Kira finds Dukat leading a Bajoran Pah-wraith cult and unmasks him when he orders a mass suicide he secretly means to survive.
A salvaged Borg vinculum infected with an alien virus unleashes the minds of people Seven assimilated, from a Klingon to a frightened child, threatening to shatter her own.
Photonic aliens mistake Tom Paris's Captain Proton serial for reality and declare war on Chaotica, forcing Janeway to play Arachnia, Queen of the Spider People.
Traumatized by the loss of his leg, Nog hides in Vic Fontaine's 1962 Las Vegas, until Vic realizes he must push his friend back to his real life.
To find a missing O'Brien, Ezri goes home to her domineering mother's mining company on New Sydney and uncovers her brother Norvo's role in a murder.
The Klingon-Cardassian Alliance of the mirror universe kidnaps Grand Nagus Zek, and its ransom forces Quark and Rom to steal the Defiant's cloaking device and cross over.
Stranded in a time-distorted sinkhole, Tuvok, Paris, and the Doctor survive with help from Noss, an alien castaway who falls for Tuvok as he suppresses his feelings.
To catch a sniper whose rifle fires through walls, Ezri calls up the persona of Joran, Dax's murderous past host, and learns to think like a killer.
Laas, a fellow Changeling sent out as an infant like Odo, urges him to abandon solids, and after he kills a Klingon, Kira frees him for Odo's sake.
Picard rebels against Starfleet when he learns it has conspired with the Son'a to forcibly relocate the Ba'ku from their youth-restoring planet, whose rings they plan to harvest.
When mobster Frankie Eyes seizes Vic's lounge through a hidden program twist, the crew plots a casino heist to set things right, and a reluctant Sisko joins in.
A wormhole seemingly leading straight to Earth enthralls the crew, but Seven, Naomi, and the Doctor discover it is the lure of a vast creature that devours ships.
At a conference on Romulus, Bashir is used in Sloan's Section 31 plot, which frames Senator Cretak and puts Section 31's secret ally Koval on the Continuing Committee.
Sisko proposes to Kasidy, Ezri finds a stranded Worf and sleeps with him before the Breen capture them both, and Dukat is surgically disguised as a Bajoran.
As crew members start breaking down, they discover they are the silver-blood duplicates from the Demon-class planet, and their Voyager disintegrates before they can get back.
Trapped in chaotic space where physics keeps shifting, Chakotay hears voices he fears are his family's hereditary madness, until he realizes aliens are trying to guide Voyager out.
Harry Kim defies regulations by falling for Tal, a woman from an isolationist Varro generational ship, and their intimacy leaves him with a glowing biological bond.
Sisko weds Kasidy despite the Prophets' warning, a disguised Dukat becomes the guide Kai Winn believes she was promised, and the Breen interrogate Worf and Ezri.
Hunted by Hazari bounty hunters, Voyager is offered rescue by the Think Tank, a cabal of brilliant aliens whose price is Seven, and Janeway turns the tables.
Janeway's raid on a Borg sphere for its transwarp coil plays into the Borg Queen's hands, and Seven surrenders to the Collective to spare Voyager, forcing a rescue.
The Dominion signs a treaty with the Breen that costs Cardassia territory, stoking Damar's resentment, as Worf and Ezri await execution and Winn chooses to follow the Pah-wraiths.
With her temper under scrutiny, Torres boards a leaking Malon freighter to stop a blast that would poison the sector, as a mutated crewman stalks its decks.
Desperate to cure Odo, Bashir and O'Brien lure Section 31's Sloan to the station and enter his dying mind to steal the cure hidden in his memories.
Coaching Seven through her first attempts at dating, the Doctor realizes he has fallen for her himself, while Neelix struggles to keep a visiting ambassador out of trouble.
Breen raids hit Earth and a new energy-draining weapon destroys the Defiant, while Damar launches a Cardassian rebellion and Winn turns to forbidden Pah-wraith texts.
Gowron's reckless war drives Worf to kill him in combat and make Martok chancellor, while Kira, Damar, and Garak steal a Breen energy-dampening weapon.
Kira, commissioned a Starfleet commander, goes with Odo and Garak to advise Damar's rebels, Bashir finds Odo carries the Founders' disease, and Gowron seizes command from Martok.
Recruited by the 29th-century timeship Relativity, Seven jumps through Voyager's history to find who planted a bomb aboard, and the saboteur proves to be a future Captain Braxton.
The Dominion crushes Damar's rebellion, forcing Kira, Damar, and Garak into hiding on Cardassia, as Quark expects to be named Grand Nagus until Zek chooses Rom.
An intelligent weapon of mass destruction seizes the Doctor's program to complete its mission, and Harry Kim must convince it the war it was built for is over.
Allies storm Cardassia and Odo's link with the Female Changeling ends the war, while Sisko thwarts Winn and Dukat's bid to free the Pah-wraiths and joins the Prophets.
Voyager meets the USS Equinox and its captain, Rudy Ransom, whose crew has survived by killing nucleogenic aliens for fuel, and he flees after stealing Voyager's shield technology.
Hunting Ransom, Janeway grows ruthless, nearly letting an Equinox crewman die and relieving Chakotay when he objects, until Ransom repents and sacrifices himself to save his remaining crew.
Three ex-drones confront Seven, who kept their minds linked after a crash years ago, and she frees them knowing they will live only a month.
Near death after a shuttle accident, Torres rides the Klingon Barge of the Dead toward Gre'thor and learns her mother's soul is condemned because of her dishonor.
Aliens from the Hierarchy spy on Voyager through the Doctor's program and mistake his heroic daydreams for reality, so he must truly play the command hologram he imagines.
Sheltering from the Turei on a scorched planet, Voyager revives the Vaadwaur after nine centuries in stasis, only to learn its new allies are would-be conquerors.
Tom Paris buys an alien shuttle from a junk dealer and falls under its possessive mind, which calls itself Alice and pulls him toward a deadly particle fountain.
An attack by cloaked Ba'Neth aliens strips Tuvok of his memories and Vulcan discipline, and Neelix helps him rebuild himself as he discovers unexpected joys.
Inside a graviton ellipse, Voyager finds the Ares IV module, lost with astronaut John Kelly on an early Mars mission, and Seven learns the value of exploration.
After absorbing Voyager's entire database at once, Seven spins a web of conspiracy theories about why the ship was stranded, turning Janeway and Chakotay against each other.
Barclay confides in Deanna Troi about his obsession with a holodeck Voyager, then risks his career to open the first live communication link with the lost ship.
Tom Paris's holographic Irish village of the 1800s becomes the crew's escape as a neutronic storm approaches, and Janeway finds herself falling for its barkeep, Michael Sullivan.
Kidnapped by the promoter Penk, Seven is forced to fight in the tsunkatse arena, where an aging Hirogen trains her while she waits for rescue.
Trapped above a world where time runs fast, Voyager becomes a fixture in the sky of a civilization that grows from primitive villages to spaceflight and frees it.
Returning from an away mission, Paris, Kim, Chakotay, and Neelix relive a massacre they never saw, memories broadcast by an alien monument so the atrocity is never forgotten.
Adolescent Borg drones cut off from the Collective hold Chakotay, Paris, Kim, and Neelix hostage on their cube, and Seven must reach the children before their leader acts.
The music-less Qomar make the Doctor a celebrity, and he resigns from Voyager to stay, only to be replaced by a hologram with an impossible vocal range.
After the crew's careless holodeck changes, the villagers of Fair Haven decide their visitors are spirit folk and turn on them, holding the Doctor captive.
Lyndsay Ballard, killed three years earlier, returns transformed into a Kobali, the species that reproduces by reviving the dead, while Seven struggles to parent the rebellious Borg children.
Seven returns Icheb to his Brunali parents, but her suspicions prove right: they engineered him as a living weapon against the Borg and mean to use him again.
Janeway takes three struggling crewmen, including the hypochondriac Telfer and the aloof Harren, on a Delta Flyer mission that turns dangerous amid dark matter.
Con artists posing as Janeway, Tuvok, and Chakotay swindle alien trading partners in Voyager's name, and the real crew runs a sting to catch them.
Stranded after a shuttle crash, Torres becomes the muse of Kelis, a poet in a pre-industrial society who turns her tales of Voyager into plays for his patron.
An aged, embittered Kes travels back to her first year aboard Voyager and helps the Vidiians attack it, determined to take her younger self home to Ocampa.
Transmitted home through the Pathfinder array, the Doctor tries to treat his dying creator, Lewis Zimmerman, who scorns the outdated program he built.
During a blackout, Neelix tells the Borg children the story behind it: an electromagnetic lifeform taken from its nebula that seized Voyager's systems in its desperation to return.
Seven discovers Unimatrix Zero, a shared dream world where drones live as individuals during regeneration, and Janeway lets herself be assimilated to help it resist the Borg Queen.
Deliberately assimilated, Janeway, Torres, and Tuvok spread a nanovirus that lets Unimatrix Zero's drones keep their individuality while awake, igniting a resistance the Borg Queen cannot crush.
In a race marking a new peace, Tom Paris flies the Delta Flyer and strains things with Torres, as a rival plots sabotage, before the couple finally marries.
Tuvok hunts whoever is attacking Voyager's former Maquis, unaware a Bajoran fanatic has conditioned him through a letter from home to be the attacker and lead a mutiny.
When Seven's cortical node begins to fail, she faces death with unexpected fear, and young Icheb offers his own implant to save her despite the risk to himself.
Stolen and sold to a hospital ship that rations care by social status, the Doctor defies its callous administrator, secretly treating the poor and even infecting him.
A holographic Barclay arrives through the Pathfinder link with a route home, but Ferengi have rigged him to lead the crew to their deaths for Seven's Borg implants.
When Lokirrim forces attack the Delta Flyer, the Doctor hides his program inside Seven's implants and indulges her senses, while aboard Voyager Tuvok battles his pon farr.
Harry Kim gets his first command aboard a crippled Kraylor ship posing as a medical transport, while Icheb misreads Torres's friendly interest as romance.
Holographic prey built with technology Janeway gave the Hirogen turn on their hunters, and the Doctor sides with their Bajoran leader, Iden, until Iden's crusade turns fanatical.
A temporal rift splinters Voyager into different eras, and Chakotay recruits a Janeway from before the ship was stranded to mend it, dodging Seska, macroviruses, and Chaotica.
Pregnant with a daughter, Torres fears the child will suffer for her Klingon traits as she did growing up, and secretly tries to alter the baby's genes.
Voyager takes aboard Nygean prisoners bound for execution, and when the Doctor cures a killer's brain defect and he feels remorse, the crew questions the death penalty.
Descendants of Klingon pilgrims who have wandered for a century decide Torres's unborn daughter is their prophesied savior, bringing their feuds and a deadly virus aboard Voyager.
Trapped in a void where stranded ships survive by preying on one another, Janeway builds a cooperative alliance, helped by Fantome, an alien who communicates through music.
Most of Voyager's crew is abducted and memory-wiped into laborers on the planet Quarra, where Janeway falls for a coworker, while Chakotay, Kim, and Neelix plot a rescue.
Chakotay goes undercover in the Quarren workforce to restore his crewmates' memories as the authorities close in, and Janeway must choose between Voyager and her new love, Jaffen.
To save his teenage son from expulsion by the Continuum, Q leaves him with Janeway to learn discipline, and the boy's reckless pranks endanger the crew.
When a publisher releases the Doctor's holonovel, a thinly veiled attack on the crew, without his consent, an arbitration hearing weighs whether a hologram can own his work.
Sent by Starfleet to recover the 21st-century probe Friendship One, Voyager finds its antimatter knowledge helped devastate an alien world, whose survivors take hostages and kill Joe Carey.
Crash-landed inside a force field protecting the primitive Ventu, Chakotay and Seven befriend the tribe, while Tom Paris serves a traffic-safety sentence for speeding on Ledos.
Hierarchy aliens abduct Janeway and demand Voyager's warp core, so the Doctor impersonates crewmates one after another to steal it, then must confess his deceptions.
Admiral Janeway travels back from the 2400s with armor and a plan to bring Voyager home through a Borg transwarp hub, sacrificing herself to cripple the Borg Queen.
Seven secretly explores emotions on the holodeck, including a romance with a simulated Chakotay, until a Borg failsafe in her implants shuts her feelings down.
Finding a Talaxian settlement in an asteroid field threatened by miners, Neelix helps it hold its ground and decides to stay with Dexa and her son.
Shinzon, Picard's clone raised in the mines of Remus, seizes Romulus and lures the Enterprise into a trap, and Data sacrifices himself to stop his thalaron weapon.
Ensign Tendi's first day aboard the USS Cerritos brings new friends Mariner, Boimler, and Rutherford, a secret order for Boimler to spy on Mariner, and an infectious outbreak.
Chasing a wayward Klingon general who gave them the slip, Boimler feels outshone by the effortless Mariner, while Rutherford quits engineering to try other jobs aboard the Cerritos.
Freeman's crackdown on buffer time leaves the overworked crew collapsing, while Mariner and Commander Ransom's feud boils over when their away team is taken captive.
Freeman assigns Mariner every miserable job aboard to make her quit, until both are trapped by runaway terraforming goo, while Tendi disrupts Lieutenant O'Connor's bid for ascension.
Boimler's too-good-to-be-true new girlfriend, Barbara, arouses Mariner's suspicion, while Tendi and Rutherford covet the flashier gear of a bigger starship.
Well-meaning Ensign Fletcher's shortcuts drag Mariner and Boimler into trouble, while Rutherford's holodeck training assistant, Badgey, turns murderous during Tendi's lesson.
Mariner strains to impress an Academy friend who now captains her own ship, while a transporter glitch leaves Boimler out of phase and quarantined among medical curiosities.
Tendi, Rutherford, Mariner, and Boimler are hauled before an alien court and made to testify about scattered incidents they glimpsed, which turn out to be connected.
Taking over Boimler's command-training holoprogram, Mariner turns it into a movie-style epic starring herself as the villain Vindicta, working through her resentment of her mother, Captain Freeman.
The Pakleds, armed with stolen tech, cripple the Cerritos and kill Lieutenant Shaxs, Mariner's secret as Freeman's daughter comes out, and Riker's Titan arrives, taking Boimler with it.
Commander Ransom absorbs a strange alien energy that turns him into a towering, godlike menace, while Mariner and Freeman awkwardly try working together as mother and daughter.
The ensigns struggle to warm to Jet Manhaver, Boimler's replacement, on a mission to a collector's hoard, while Boimler finds Riker's Titan more intense than he bargained for.
Mariner and Tendi retrieve a keepsake for Dr. T'Ana, Boimler schemes to meet the visiting Tom Paris, and Rutherford is unnerved when the late Shaxs turns up alive.
Checking reports of a mugato, the venomous horned ape, on a remote planet, the Cerritos away team runs into poachers who hunt the creatures.
Rumors of a legendary, exclusive Starfleet bash send Mariner and Boimler searching, while the bridge crew escorts a Doopler envoy whose species copies itself whenever it feels embarrassed.
Anomaly consolidation day stirs mixed feelings among the ensigns, while Captain Freeman seeks a peace deal with the Pakleds on their homeworld and a Pakled spy slips aboard.
Mariner and Boimler crash on a barren planet with AGIMUS, a megalomaniacal computer they were transporting, while Billups has to outshine an old rival as an engineer.
A visiting consultant puts the Cerritos through drills that swap the ensigns' duties with the bridge crew's, and Boimler throws himself too fully into a Borg assimilation scenario.
On a long warp haul, Boimler seeks a friend on the bridge, while junior officers aboard a Klingon ship and a Vulcan ship live out parallel days.
The Cerritos supports another starship's first contact mission, which goes awry, and the crew's triumph ends with Captain Freeman arrested for the destruction of the Pakled homeworld.
While Captain Freeman stands trial, accused of destroying the Pakled homeworld, her daughter Mariner leads her friends on an unauthorized mission to clear the captain's name.
Mariner questions how Commander Ransom chooses his away teams during a mission to a tropical paradise, while Boimler decides to take a daring leap in his career.
Stone orbs at a remote science outpost start making people's fantasies real, just as Tendi begins her first day training to become a senior science officer.
Old grudges flare between Delta Shift and the trio of Mariner, Boimler, and Tendi, while the Cerritos engineers are ordered onto mandatory relaxation leave.
Mariner and Boimler try to sign up new Starfleet recruits at an interstellar career fair, while Rutherford sets out to test his own limits.
The Cerritos makes an unplanned stop at Deep Space 9, where Freeman meets Colonel Kira and the ensigns explore the station's storied Promenade.
Peanut Hamper, the exocomp who abandoned the Cerritos in battle, tries to redeem herself among kindly aliens on a remote world, but old habits prove hard to shake.
Boimler shoots Crisis Point 2: Paradoxus, a holodeck sequel he fears can never match the original, with his friends pulled into the production.
A reporter embeds aboard the Cerritos, and Captain Freeman, anxious about how her crew will be portrayed, struggles to keep things under control.
To save the California-class ships from retirement, the Cerritos races an automated Texas-class starship on a mission contest, only for the drone ship to turn hostile.
The ensigns help ferry the retired USS Voyager to a museum, where a transporter mishap fuses two Cerritos officers into one, echoing an infamous incident from its past.

records.ti: I Have No Bones Yet I Must Flee
records.lg: Now lieutenants, Mariner schemes to get herself demoted while Rutherford chases a promotion and Boimler moves into new quarters, as a cute, bone-sucking Moopsy runs loose aboard.
records.ma: I Have No Bones Yet I Must Flee (episode)

records.lg: Boimler takes charge of his first away mission, exploring a vast alien megastructure, and quickly discovers how much responsibility the job carries.
Summoned home to Orion for a family wedding, Tendi brings Mariner along and must face her family and the past she left to join Starfleet.
A party-loving Betazoid delegation visits the Cerritos, and its uninhibited mood spreads through the crew with unruly results.
The Cerritos visits Ferenginar as Grand Nagus Rom weighs bringing the Ferengi into the Federation, and Captain Freeman works to seal the deal amid Ferengi-style hospitality.
Three rogue machines resurface to plague the Cerritos crew: Rutherford's hologram Badgey, the scheming computer AGIMUS, and the treacherous exocomp Peanut Hamper.
Trapped in a cave during a routine mission, the friends pass the time trading tales of their earlier cave misadventures.
Worried about Mariner's reckless streak, Captain Freeman gives the ensigns an ultra-safe assignment, but Mariner's self-destructive behavior pulls her toward real danger.
Mariner confronts her past when the raider destroying ships proves to be led by Nick Locarno, the disgraced former Starfleet cadet she once knew.
A quantum fissure brings the Cerritos face to face with a duplicate ship from another reality, crewed by alternate versions of its own officers.
Tendi scrambles to defuse a conflict, while Mariner and Boimler set out to thwart a scheme by profit-hungry capitalists.
On a visit to a luxury resort in space, the friends end up hunting runaway nanites loose on the premises.
Dr. Migleemo turns up the heat in the kitchen, while Mariner nurses a grudge and plots a revenge best served cold.
A visit to the notoriously run-down Starbase 80 finds Ransom overdoing the disinfectant gel and Mariner growing paranoid that she has been cursed.
A troubled ensign partners with Mariner, while the Cerritos plays host to negotiations between two rival civilizations.
A covert survey of a pre-warp society turns into a girls' trip for the Cerritos women sent undercover among the locals.
While the friends throw a pumpkin-carving party below, the Cerritos's senior officers get a turn in the spotlight on the upper decks.
William Boimler, the transporter double now captaining the USS Anaximander, commands alternate versions of Garak, Bashir, T'Pol, and Dax to seal the quantum fissures tearing at the multiverse.
The quantum fissure crisis comes to a head as the Cerritos crew makes its final stand to keep the multiverse from collapsing, closing out their adventures.
Young prisoners on the mining colony Tars Lamora, led by Dal, commandeer the derelict starship Protostar and escape the Diviner, taking his daughter Gwyn along against her will.
With Dal as self-appointed captain, the untrained crew takes its first lessons from Hologram Janeway, then must steer the Protostar off a deadly cosmic collision course.
On their first away mission, the crew explores a planet that conjures each member's deepest desires, only to find the living world is luring them in to feed.
Stranded on a hostile planet, the crew must rely on their captive Gwyn to survive, while the Diviner's relentless robot enforcer Drednok closes in.
Dal runs the Kobayashi Maru on the newfound holodeck with a crew of simulated Starfleet legends to prove himself, while Gwyn searches for her place aboard.
Dal's old mentor, Nandi, talks him into using the crew's Starfleet guise to swindle a newly contacted species, and the scheme shows why Starfleet's protocols exist.
An anomaly splinters the Protostar into pockets of different time, and Hologram Janeway must bring each isolated crew member back in sync before the ship destroys itself.
Giving up their dream of reaching Starfleet, the crew turns back to Tars Lamora to free the prisoners they left behind, a seemingly unwinnable mission.
When their liberation plan unravels, the crew improvises to free Tars Lamora's prisoners, and Gwyn learns her father's grim purpose for the Protostar.
Seeking asylum at a remote Federation relay station, the crew discovers the Protostar carries a hidden weapon that turns nearby Starfleet systems against themselves.
Exploring a dormant Borg cube, the crew stirs its drones back to life, and Zero makes a desperate gamble to keep everyone from assimilation.
A distress call leads the crew to a colony whose whole culture imitates a long-ago Starfleet visit, and saving it means playing the roles it expects.
Trying to book passage into Federation space, the crew unknowingly crosses paths with the real Vice Admiral Janeway, who is hunting the Protostar.
Caught in the Romulan Neutral Zone, Dal and his friends meet a rogue geneticist who reveals that Dal was engineered from the DNA of many species.
As a Starfleet admiral probes the Protostar crew's pasts, the Diviner recalls how his homeworld, Solum, was ruined, and the vengeful mission it inspired.
A mysterious malfunction traps the crew in the holodeck, where they can no longer tell what is programmed from what is real.
To warn Starfleet about the weapon aboard their ship, the crew tries a risky experiment that swaps Dal's mind with that of Vice Admiral Janeway.
With a Federation armada gathered around the Protostar, the crew races to stop the weapon inside it from turning Starfleet's ships against one another.
The crew sacrifices the Protostar to shield the fleet from its weapon, and as the Diviner's scheme collapses, the young outlaws earn a future in Starfleet.
Now Starfleet trainees, Dal and his friends join Admiral Janeway aboard the USS Voyager-A to study the rift left by the Protostar, though Dal is restless for action.
Gwyn meets an old adversary on her ancestral world, Solum, as Janeway confides to the cadets what their mission to the rift truly puts at risk.
Dal's team slips through the time rift to comb Solum for the missing Chakotay, while Gwyn, backed by her father, defies the militant Asencia.
Back aboard Voyager and closely watched, the cadets work to decode a secret message that their unknown benefactor entrusted to Murf.
Planning to steal the Infinity before it is scrapped, Dal and the crew program holographic doubles of themselves to cover their absence aboard Voyager.
A shortcut through a Borg transwarp conduit leaves Dal and his friends under the thumb of a demanding Kazon.

records.ti: Is There in Beauty No Truth?
records.lg: A detour to a colony of noncorporeal beings brings Zero an offer of a physical body, while Janeway uncovers what Dal is really planning.
records.ma: Is There in Beauty No Truth? (episode)

records.ti: The Devourer of All Things, Part I
records.lg: Reaching the coordinates at last, the Infinity crew finds a hidden planet and learns who their mysterious messenger has been all along.
records.ma: The Devourer of All Things, Part I (episode)

records.ti: The Devourer of All Things, Part II
records.lg: Fleeing pursuers that erase whatever they touch from time, the Infinity's crew and a new ally hunt for an escape route while Voyager mounts a rescue.
records.ma: The Devourer of All Things, Part II (episode)

records.ti: Last Flight of the Protostar, Part I
records.lg: Wesley Crusher's timely help leads the cadets to the lost Protostar, but its marooned guardian, Chakotay, is wary of their offer of rescue.
records.ma: Last Flight of the Protostar, Part I (episode)

records.ti: Last Flight of the Protostar, Part II
records.lg: Chakotay and the cadets hatch a risky plan to get the grounded Protostar airborne again, one that requires the starship to sail before it can fly.
records.ma: Last Flight of the Protostar, Part II (episode)

records.lg: Collecting bosonite on a desolate planet, the crew is overrun by vicious, genetically engineered tribbles bred there by a Klingon researcher.
When the Protostar links up with Voyager again, the crew starts skipping from one alternate reality to the next, the mirror universe among them.
With their mission nearly done, the two crews of Voyager and the Protostar face Asencia, their enemy from Solum, who returns with startling new abilities.
Outgunned by Asencia's uncannily advanced weapons, the allied crews resort to a string of gambles that leave the cadets in serious danger.
As the Federation and Solum edge toward war, Gwyn talks the cadets into an undercover operation to collect intelligence and free her father, Ilthuran.
Janeway schemes to break her crew out of Asencia's prison, where they are locked up alongside a furious being taken from the Loom.
Cornered, Asencia unleashes a total offensive against the Federation that could wipe out subspace, as Wesley leads the cadets in a bid to set the timeline right.
The petty feud between schoolgirls Kima and Lil is swept aside on First Contact Day 2385, when rogue synths attack Mars and destroy its shipyards.
The cadets take on Asencia in a decisive fight over Solum's fate and the timeline, until a devastating alien incursion throws their final plan into chaos.
Retired to his vineyard, Picard is sought out by Dahj, a woman hunted by assassins, and after her death learns she was Data's synthetic daughter, with a twin.
Rebuffed by Starfleet, Picard investigates Dahj's origins with synthetic researcher Agnes Jurati and turns to estranged former aide Raffi Musiker, as a secret Romulan cabal tracks his search.
Unaware she is synthetic, Soji works on a Romulan-held Borg cube under Hugh, while Picard, rebuffed by Raffi, hires pilot Cristóbal Rios to find Bruce Maddox.
Picard detours to Vashti, where he resettled Romulan refugees, and enlists Elnor, the Qowat Milat-raised youth he left behind, before Seven of Nine arrives to rescue La Sirena.
On Freecloud, Picard's crew cons crime boss Bjayzl to free Bruce Maddox, Seven of Nine avenges Icheb, and Jurati secretly kills Maddox.
Facing his Borg trauma, Picard boards the Romulan-held cube to reach Soji, as Narek uses a Romulan puzzle box to pry her homeworld's location from her memories.
At Nepenthe, the home of Riker and Troi, Picard helps Soji come to terms with herself, while on the cube Narissa kills Hugh and Elnor makes a stand.
Picard's crew learns the Zhat Vash, a secret Romulan sect, orchestrated the Mars attack to stop synthetic life, while Seven links with the cube's Borg to fight Narissa.
Reaching Coppelius, the synthetics' hidden homeworld, Picard's crew meets Altan Soong and the android Sutra, who plans to summon machine allies as a Romulan armada closes in.
Picard persuades Soji to halt the synthetics' beacon as Riker's fleet faces down the Romulans, then dies, wakes in a synthetic body, and grants Data his final wish.
A Borg ship emerging from a space anomaly asks to join the Federation, and Picard's reunion with his crew ends with the Stargazer's self-destruct and Q's return.
Q strands Picard in a dystopian 2401 ruled by the Confederation of Earth, where he rounds up his displaced crew and seizes a captive Borg Queen to escape.
Elnor dies as the crew escapes to 2024 Los Angeles to find a mysterious Watcher, while Picard and Jurati extract what they can from the Borg Queen.
Answering Beverly Crusher's coded plea, Picard and Riker talk their way onto the USS Titan and find her hiding with a grown son, Jack, as Vadic closes in.
Aboard the Titan, Picard learns Jack is his son as Vadic demands the young man's surrender, while Raffi, tracking a stolen weapon, finds her mysterious handler is Worf.
Picard reels at being a father as the Titan plays cat and mouse with Vadic inside a nebula, and Raffi and Worf trace the plot to renegade Changelings.
Trapped and powerless inside the nebula, the Titan drifts toward destruction as Picard, Riker, and Shaw confront old wounds, until the nebula's hidden nature offers an escape.
Intercepted by Starfleet, Picard must learn whether Ro Laren, his old officer turned Intelligence agent, is friend or Changeling, and she gives her life to expose Starfleet's infiltration.
Now fugitives, the Titan crew enlists Geordi La Forge to break into Daystrom Station, where they learn Picard's original body was stolen and find a revived Data.
To learn Vadic's motives, Picard lures her into a trap aboard the Titan, uncovering Starfleet's wartime experiments on Changelings, but the gambit backfires and she seizes the ship.
Vadic, holding the Titan's bridge, demands Jack for the crew's lives, while Data battles Lore for their shared body and, winning, helps the crew retake the ship.
Jack's visions lead to the Borg Queen, whose Changeling-aided plot turns Starfleet's young crews into drones on Frontier Day, and Picard's old crew takes the restored Enterprise-D.
Picard's old crew takes the Enterprise-D against the Borg Queen's cube hidden in Jupiter to free Jack and the fleet, and Seven inherits a new Enterprise.
Decades apart in time, Voyager's crew and the cadets aboard the Infinity join forces to keep Gwyn alive, and an unknown messenger makes contact with her.
Seven hundred years on, a Kyrian museum portrays Voyager as a murderous warship, and a reactivated backup of the Doctor fights to correct the record amid Kyrian-Vaskan tensions.
Landing alone in 3188, Burnham falls in with courier Cleveland Booker, learns the Burn has shattered the Federation, and finds a lone loyalist, Sahil, still guarding its flag.
Discovery crash-lands on an ice world, Saru and Tilly seek help from a hostile mining town until Georgiou intervenes, and Burnham finds them after a year's search.
Captained by Saru, Discovery finds an isolationist Earth outside the Federation, defuses its feud with raiders from Titan, and meets Adira, a human host to a Trill symbiont.
Burnham takes Adira to Trill to unlock the symbiont's memories, which reveal Adira's late partner Gray, while Saru hosts a crew dinner that erupts into tension.
Discovery reaches Federation headquarters and a wary Admiral Vance, then earns its place by helping a stricken seed-vault ship while the enigmatic Kovich interrogates Georgiou.
Burnham and Georgiou go rogue to free Book from an Emerald Chain labor camp and recover a black box holding Burn clues, costing Burnham her first officer post.
On Ni'Var, the reunified Vulcan-Romulan world, Burnham argues for access to its Burn research with her mother, now a Qowat Milat nun, as her advocate.
Discovery accompanies Book to Kwejian, where the Emerald Chain's Osyraa exploits a crop-destroying swarm to pressure his people, while Stamets and Adira keep hunting the Burn's origin.
With Georgiou's body breaking down, Discovery takes her to Dannus V, where a gatekeeper named Carl sends her back into the mirror universe of her past.
Reliving her reign in the Terran Empire, Georgiou meets a coup with newfound mercy, then learns Carl is the Guardian of Forever and leaves Discovery for good.
Inside the Verubin Nebula, Saru, Culber, and Burnham find Su'Kal, a Kelpien raised alone on a wrecked ship, whose anguish caused the Burn, as Osyraa moves on Discovery.
Osyraa brings the captured Discovery to Federation headquarters and offers Vance an alliance, while Burnham slips back aboard to retake the ship from Emerald Chain forces.
Burnham retakes Discovery and kills Osyraa, Book steers the spore drive to rescue the away team from the nebula, and Saru steps aside so Burnham can take command.
Captain Burnham's Discovery rescues a space station damaged by a gravitational anomaly under President Rillak's eye, and the same phenomenon then obliterates Book's homeworld, Kwejian.
Saru returns to help study the anomaly, and Burnham joins a grieving Book on a flight into it while helping him face the loss of his family.
Burnham and Tilly pursue a renegade Qowat Milat who killed a Starfleet officer, while Stamets works to predict the anomaly and Gray finally receives a synthetic body.
Tilly and Adira's cadet training flight crash-lands on a planetoid, Burnham joins Ni'Var's talks on rejoining the Federation, and Tilly decides to leave Discovery to teach.
As the anomaly nears a stranded colony, Burnham and Book scramble to get everyone out, while the brilliant, abrasive Ruon Tarka joins Saru and Stamets.
Trapped inside a subspace rift left by the anomaly, Discovery struggles to escape as its AI Zora feels fear and Book sees visions of his father.
A galactic summit debates attacking or contacting the anomaly's makers, Book and Tarka break ranks, and Kovich tests whether the newly sentient Zora is a threat.
Guessing Book's next move, Burnham seeks him out at a spot they knew as couriers and gets pulled into a contest over a dangerous weapon.
With Nhan aboard to keep Burnham in check, Discovery chases Book and Tarka to the anomaly, but their weapon destroys it and Species 10-C promptly makes another.
Discovery crosses the Galactic Barrier in search of Species 10-C, while Book discovers that Tarka's true goal is to reach another universe and reunite with a lost friend.
